<!doctype html>

NEWS FROM THE POLITICAL REVOLUTION

HEADLINES: Meet Our Candidates | Establishment vs Progressives | Primaries
Underway! | Tom Steyer Talks to Our Members | Exciting New Endorsements | CPC
Affordability Agenda | & MORE!

★ ★ ★

The 2026 primaries are happening right now.

The Supreme Court just gutted the Voting Rights Act. Dark money is flooding our
elections. And the Democratic establishment is intervening in key races to try
to block the very progressives we need to win.

But here’s what they’re missing: the energy is on our side.

Across the country, we’re seeing it firsthand as we hit the streets to get out
the vote for a new generation of candidates who have stepped up — inspired by
Bernie and ready to fight for real change. [ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/38113?t=1011&akid=10709%2E5885482%2Es_Th1B ]See all of our endorsed candidates
here!

Yes, we’re working to elect bold progressives to Congress. But Our Revolution is
also doing something no one else is: building power from the ground up.

This is how we build the bench. We stood with some of the candidates below when
they first ran for school board, and now they’re running for mayor, state
senate, and beyond.

These are movement candidates — rejecting corporate money, building grassroots
momentum, and generating the energy we’ll need to defeat MAGA in November.

We’ve shown we can put millions in the streets — now we need to get millions out
the vote. [ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/35232?t=1012&akid=10709%2E5885482%2Es_Th1B ]If you can, chip in a donation of any amount to help us call, text,
and knock doors ahead of election day.

★ ★ ★

ELECT PROGRESSIVES

★ ★ ★

On Monday, candidates from some of the top races in the country joined our
[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/38202?t=1013&akid=10709%2E5885482%2Es_Th1B ]LIVE National Organize to Win Town Hall to speak directly with our movement
about what it will take to win.

While we’ve never endorsed a billionaire before, Tom Steyer is running to
deliver on our top progressive priorities — including Medicare for All, taxing
extreme wealth, and taking on ICE and utility monopolies — with a focus on
making California affordable for working people.

He has been a partner to the movement, investing in climate advocacy and
grassroots organizing while taking on corporate power. As Tom told our members,
“We can’t nibble around the edges — we have to take on the system head-on and
deliver real change for working people.” [ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/38113?t=1014&akid=10709%2E5885482%2Es_Th1B ]See our full slate of California
endorsements here!

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/38203?t=1015&akid=10709%2E5885482%2Es_Th1B ]JOIN OUR PHONEBANK TEAM TO ELECT BOLD PROGRESSIVES!

★ ★ ★

On the call, Janeese Lewis George talked about her run for Mayor of Washington,
D.C. and what it will mean to lead the nation’s capital while Trump occupies the
city.

As a DC Council member and proud democratic socialist, Janeese has built her
career by fighting for universal childcare, social housing, labor protections,
and making the city affordable — in a race where corporate developers and
establishment forces are lining up against her.

As Janeese told our members, “If we want to protect our communities, we need
leadership that won’t back down — even when the pressure is coming straight from
the White House.”

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/35232?t=1016&akid=10709%2E5885482%2Es_Th1B ]Donate now to power our grassroots organizing and help true fighters win the
primaries this spring so we can beat MAGA in November.

★ ★ ★

Eric Jones talked on the organizing call Monday about his campaign for Congress
in CA-04 — and why it’s time to challenge decades of status quo leadership.

Running in Napa Valley against a 27-year Democratic incumbent, Eric is stepping
up to take on corporate power and deliver real results for working families.

An entrepreneur and nonprofit founder, he’s focused on cutting everyday costs,
expanding affordable childcare and elder care, and putting money back in
people’s pockets — while holding corporations like PG&E accountable and pushing
for stronger wildfire prevention.

As Eric told our members, “This district deserves leadership that’s willing to
take on corruption and fight for working people — not protect the system that’s
failing them.”

★ ★ ★

On the call, we were also proud to endorse Matt Dunlap for Congress in Maine’s
2nd District.

A former Secretary of State and Bernie 2016 co-chair, Matt has spent decades
defending voting rights — including taking on Trump’s voter suppression
commission — and fighting for real economic justice.

But as Matt shared with our members, even after his opponent (Jared Golden, the
most conservative Democrat in Congress) stepped aside, Hakeem Jeffries and the
DCCC rushed to endorse another candidate rather than support a proven
progressive.

That’s fine — Matt is building a powerful grassroots campaign and leading the
polls with our movement at his back.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/38203?t=1017&akid=10709%2E5885482%2Es_Th1B ]HELP USPHONE BANK!

★ ★ ★

We’re also proud to endorse Aisha Wahab for Congress in CA-04.

Born to Afghan refugees, Aisha made history as the first Muslim elected to the
California State Senate — now she’s running to bring bold leadership to
Washington as she takes on the establishment in an open race to replace
disgraced Eric Swalwell.

Backed by leaders like Pramila Jayapal, Greg Casar, and Maxwell Frost, Aisha is
building a strong grassroots campaign focused on affordability and housing in
one of the most expensive regions in the country.

As she told our members, this race is about whether the district elects a real
progressive who will fight for people — or more of the same politics that put
corporate interests first.

★ ★ ★

On the call, Our Revolution ally Brandee Marckmann talked about why San
Francisco needs to stop treating public schools like a budget problem and start
investing in them as the foundation of strong communities.

As a community organizer, Brandee has been on the frontlines defending public
education — founding the SF Education Alliance to push back against
privatization and fight for schools that serve all students.

She’s running to support educators, expand equity, and build community-driven
schools that work for working families — not corporate interests.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/35232?t=1018&akid=10709%2E5885482%2Es_Th1B ]This is a critical election year, and we have a lot of work ahead of us.
Donate to make sure we have the resources to get these elect working class
fighters and defeat MAGA in the Midterms.

★ ★ ★

MORE NEW ENDORSEMENTS!

★ ★ ★

Big Tech billionaires are pouring money into politics to stop regulation and
protect their power. Alex Bores is one of the few politicians actually taking
them on — and he has our support for Congress in NY-12.

A leader on some of the strongest AI accountability legislation in the country,
Alex is fighting for a future where technology serves people — not corporate
monopolies and billionaires.

He’s running on a bold agenda to take on concentrated wealth, political
corruption, and corporate power — and bring a new generation of progressive
leadership to Congress. [ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/38113?t=1019&akid=10709%2E5885482%2Es_Th1B ]Check out more New York endorsements here.

★ ★ ★

For decades, this Georgia Congress seat has been represented by the status quo.
Now voters have a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to send a new generation of
progressive leadership to Congress with Everton Blair for Congress in GA-13.

A former teacher and school board chair, Everton is running to fight for working
families — with a bold agenda centered on Medicare for All, affordable housing,
childcare, fully funded public schools, and good-paying jobs.

As Everton told our movement: “GA-13 deserves representation that will fight to
put people over profit at every turn. Now is our time.”

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/38203?t=1020&akid=10709%2E5885482%2Es_Th1B ]HELP US PHONE BANK!

★ ★ ★

ACTION CENTER

★ ★ ★

NEW AFFORDABILITY AGENDA

Last week, Our Revolution activists joined Reps. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Chuy
Garcia, Greg Casar, and other leaders in the Congressional Progressive Caucus to
launch a bold new Affordability Agenda.

This is exactly the kind of platform Democrats should be running on in 2026 —
and passing into law in 2027.

From lowering prescription drug prices and childcare costs to taking on
corporate price gouging and utility monopolies, this agenda is about putting
money back in people’s pockets and taking power away from billionaires.

At a time when families are being squeezed, we’re standing with leaders who are
fighting for real solutions — not more politics as usual.

★ ★ ★

Nine courageous activists put their bodies on the line and were arrested in the
fight to hold politicians accountable this week as we wrapped up the March on
Harrisburg.

Our Revolution was proud to join the 4-day march from Reading, PA to the State
Capital, where we addressed press and voices echoed the call: Which side are you
on?

Working people are struggling to get by while billionaires buy influence with
massive checks, lavish gifts, and secret Super PAC money. We marched to say
enough is enough: Stop the billionaire bribes and pass a ban on political
‘gifts.’

★ ★ ★

TELL DEMS: NO OLIGARCH MONEY IN PRIMARIES

Ultra-rich powerbrokers are flooding the primaries with corporate cash from AI,
Crypto, and AIPAC. Our movement candidates are rejecting dark and corporate
money, but we need the Democratic Party to stand with us.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/35247?t=1021&akid=10709%2E5885482%2Es_Th1B ]Add your name to demand a ban on Dark Money in ALL Democratic primaries in
2026!

Our Revolution is focused on building grassroots power to Fight Trump & the

1. Fight Trump’s Oligarch Agenda - from Capitol Hill to City Halls
2. Elect Anti-Oligarch Champions up and down the ballot
3. Get Oligarch Money out of Politics and uplift the grassroots

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/35232?t=1022&akid=10709%2E5885482%2Es_Th1B ]We take ZERO money from corporate donors. We rely on the grassroots to keep
up this great work. Chip in a donation today!

Big Money from AIPAC, AI, and Crypto is pouring in against our endorsed

Their money can only go so far. We can out-organize the special interests by

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/37508?t=1023&akid=10709%2E5885482%2Es_Th1B ]PHONEBANK WITH OUR TEAM

MIDTERMS MERCH!

The 2026 midterms are pivotal to take power back from Trump and the oligarchs

All of our candidates reject dark and corporate PAC money — and they’ve all

The Supreme Court just gutted the Voting Rights Act. Dark money is flooding our elections. And the Democratic establishment is intervening in key races to try to block the very progressives we need to win. But here’s what they’re missing: the energy is on our side. Across the country, we’re seeing it firsthand as we hit the streets to get out the vote for a new generation of candidates who have stepped up — inspired by Bernie and ready to fight for real change. [ ]See all of our endorsed candidates here! Yes, we’re working to elect bold progressives to Congress. But Our Revolution is also doing something no one else is: building power from the ground up. This is how we build the bench. We stood with some of the candidates below when they first ran for school board, and now they’re running for mayor, state senate, and beyond. These are movement candidates — rejecting corporate money, building grassroots momentum, and generating the energy we’ll need to defeat MAGA in November. We’ve shown we can put millions in the streets — now we need to get millions out the vote. [ ]If you can, chip in a donation of any amount to help us call, text, and knock doors ahead of election day. ★ ★ ★ ELECT PROGRESSIVES ★ ★ ★ On Monday, candidates from some of the top races in the country joined our [ ]LIVE National Organize to Win Town Hall to speak directly with our movement about what it will take to win. While we’ve never endorsed a billionaire before, Tom Steyer is running to deliver on our top progressive priorities — including Medicare for All, taxing extreme wealth, and taking on ICE and utility monopolies — with a focus on making California affordable for working people. He has been a partner to the movement, investing in climate advocacy and grassroots organizing while taking on corporate power. As Tom told our members, “We can’t nibble around the edges — we have to take on the system head-on and deliver real change for working people.” [ ]See our full slate of California endorsements here! [ ]JOIN OUR PHONEBANK TEAM TO ELECT BOLD PROGRESSIVES! ★ ★ ★ On the call, Janeese Lewis George talked about her run for Mayor of Washington, D.C. and what it will mean to lead the nation’s capital while Trump occupies the city. As a DC Council member and proud democratic socialist, Janeese has built her career by fighting for universal childcare, social housing, labor protections, and making the city affordable — in a race where corporate developers and establishment forces are lining up against her. As Janeese told our members, “If we want to protect our communities, we need leadership that won’t back down — even when the pressure is coming straight from the White House.” [ ]Donate now to power our grassroots organizing and help true fighters win the primaries this spring so we can beat MAGA in November. ★ ★ ★ Eric Jones talked on the organizing call Monday about his campaign for Congress in CA-04 — and why it’s time to challenge decades of status quo leadership. Running in Napa Valley against a 27-year Democratic incumbent, Eric is stepping up to take on corporate power and deliver real results for working families. An entrepreneur and nonprofit founder, he’s focused on cutting everyday costs, expanding affordable childcare and elder care, and putting money back in people’s pockets — while holding corporations like PG&E accountable and pushing for stronger wildfire prevention. As Eric told our members, “This district deserves leadership that’s willing to take on corruption and fight for working people — not protect the system that’s failing them.” ★ ★ ★ On the call, we were also proud to endorse Matt Dunlap for Congress in Maine’s 2nd District. A former Secretary of State and Bernie 2016 co-chair, Matt has spent decades defending voting rights — including taking on Trump’s voter suppression commission — and fighting for real economic justice. But as Matt shared with our members, even after his opponent (Jared Golden, the most conservative Democrat in Congress) stepped aside, Hakeem Jeffries and the DCCC rushed to endorse another candidate rather than support a proven progressive. That’s fine — Matt is building a powerful grassroots campaign and leading the polls with our movement at his back. [ ]HELP USPHONE BANK! ★ ★ ★ We’re also proud to endorse Aisha Wahab for Congress in CA-04. Born to Afghan refugees, Aisha made history as the first Muslim elected to the California State Senate — now she’s running to bring bold leadership to Washington as she takes on the establishment in an open race to replace disgraced Eric Swalwell. Backed by leaders like Pramila Jayapal, Greg Casar, and Maxwell Frost, Aisha is building a strong grassroots campaign focused on affordability and housing in one of the most expensive regions in the country. As she told our members, this race is about whether the district elects a real progressive who will fight for people — or more of the same politics that put corporate interests first. ★ ★ ★ On the call, Our Revolution ally Brandee Marckmann talked about why San Francisco needs to stop treating public schools like a budget problem and start investing in them as the foundation of strong communities. As a community organizer, Brandee has been on the frontlines defending public education — founding the SF Education Alliance to push back against privatization and fight for schools that serve all students. She’s running to support educators, expand equity, and build community-driven schools that work for working families — not corporate interests. [ ]This is a critical election year, and we have a lot of work ahead of us. Donate to make sure we have the resources to get these elect working class fighters and defeat MAGA in the Midterms. ★ ★ ★ MORE NEW ENDORSEMENTS! ★ ★ ★ Big Tech billionaires are pouring money into politics to stop regulation and protect their power. A leader on some of the strongest AI accountability legislation in the country, Alex is fighting for a future where technology serves people — not corporate monopolies and billionaires. He’s running on a bold agenda to take on concentrated wealth, political corruption, and corporate power — and bring a new generation of progressive leadership to Congress. [ ]Check out more New York endorsements here. ★ ★ ★ For decades, this Georgia Congress seat has been represented by the status quo. Now voters have a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to send a new generation of progressive leadership to Congress with Everton Blair for Congress in GA-13. A former teacher and school board chair, Everton is running to fight for working families — with a bold agenda centered on Medicare for All, affordable housing, childcare, fully funded public schools, and good-paying jobs. | Peter,
On Wed, April 29th, SCOTUS struck down the foundation of the VRA, the legislation that ended Jim Crow, making it permissible to create new segregated districts denying black voters the opportunity for equal representation.
Then on Thurs, April 30th, everything changed. MAGA crossed a rubicon and did something that had never before seen in American political history:
They declared a "state of emergency", suspended our upcoming House elections, and began the process of erasing our two black districts.
With GOP super majorities in our State House, a conservative state supreme court, and a MAGA Governor, all seemed lost. As one of the least funded parties in the nation our options were extremely limited. But then something unexpected happened. Hundreds of thousands of Democrats from across the nation began to join our ranks:

Our Actblue account an hour after the announcement of the Governor's decision to suspend our House election.
On April 30th we all became Louisiana Democrats. Whether you were in Boulder, CO, or New Philadelphia, Ohio, our plight became a rallying cry for Democrats everywhere.
In the days that followed we raised more than our party had raised in entire election cycles.
Now we are headed into this fight with real firepower. We will be able launch an unprecedented counter-disinformation campaign (MAGA has convinced millions of Louisanans that the entire election has been canceled when in reality it is only the House races). But all of this only staunches the bleeding. The real fight ahead will be the fight to defend incumbent Congressman Cleo Fields (D-LA) the Democrat whose black majority district is in the bullseye of MAGA's Jim Crow redistricting scheme, and Congressman Troy Carter (D-LA) whose district could be next.
We have to spend the next four months ensuring that these Congressman can hold out against the overwhelming odds they now likely face. And If they don't survive, MAGA's gerrymandering scheme gets them two seats closer to weathering the midterms that should've been their undoing.
Please God let the levees hold against the rising tide. [Can you rush a donation to help us defend Louisiana's incumbent Democratic Congressmen from the unimaginable onslaught they now face? Our average donation is $25, many give more, some give less. clean_body: When the Louisiana Governor canceled the May 16th House elections so he could dismantle black districts, our plight became a rallying cry for Democrats everywhere. | | | | | == | Peter, On Wed, April 29th, SCOTUS struck down the foundation of the VRA, the legislation that ended Jim Crow, making it permissible to create new segregated districts denying black voters the opportunity for equal representation. Then on Thurs, April 30th, everything changed. MAGA crossed a rubicon and did something that had never before seen in American political history: They declared a "state of emergency", suspended our upcoming House elections, and began the process of erasing our two black districts. With GOP super majorities in our State House, a conservative state supreme court, and a MAGA Governor, all seemed lost. As one of the least funded parties in the nation our options were extremely limited. But then something unexpected happened. Hundreds of thousands of Democrats from across the nation began to join our ranks: | | == Our Actblue account an hour after the announcement of the Governor's decision to suspend our House election. On April 30th we all became Louisiana Democrats. Whether you were in Boulder, CO, or New Philadelphia, Ohio, our plight became a rallying cry for Democrats everywhere. In the days that followed we raised more than our party had raised in entire election cycles. Now we are headed into this fight with real firepower. We will be able launch an unprecedented counter-disinformation campaign (MAGA has convinced millions of Louisanans that the entire election has been canceled when in reality it is only the House races). But all of this only staunches the bleeding. The real fight ahead will be the fight to defend incumbent Congressman Cleo Fields (D-LA) the Democrat whose black majority district is in the bullseye of MAGA's Jim Crow redistricting scheme, and Congressman Troy Carter (D-LA) whose district could be next. We have to spend the next four months ensuring that these Congressman can hold out against the overwhelming odds they now likely face. And If they don't survive, MAGA's gerrymandering scheme gets them two seats closer to weathering the midterms that should've been their undoing. Please God let the levees hold against the rising tide. == If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | == | | == | | == | | == | | == | | == | == | We will never forget what you did for us when all seemed lost. Wait times have increased at 71% of the hospitals they have data for, and these increases are hitting the newest generation of Veterans especially hard.
#
Peter:
Earlier this week, the Vet Voice Foundation released one hell of a study. They studied wait time data from VA facilities across the country, and what they found should shock you.
Wait times have increased at 71% of the hospitals they have data for, and these increases are hitting the newest generation of Veterans especially hard. Neurology, where Veterans get care for traumatic brain injuries, sees average wait times of 76 days. Oncology, cancer treatment for toxic exposures, 46 days. Pulmonology, treatment for lungs damaged by burn pits, 45 days. The VA standard for care? 28 days.
The VA isn’t broken — it’s being dismantled by the Republican Party and Donald Trump. 30,000 VA staff positions have been eliminated since Trump took office, and 90% of VA facilities are short of doctors. All of this is by design, all of it was in Project 2025, and all of it contributes to the same goal: Privatization.
Trump and MAGA want to line their pockets with money that’s been promised to spend on Veterans' health care. They’re going to fail, just like they always have, because VoteVets is going to raise hell.

Because the fastest path to a federal judgeship or top DOJ job isn’t
public service or legal excellence anymore. It’s being Donald Trump’s
personal lawyer and proving your loyalty.

Since returning to office, Trump has elevated at least 10 of his former
personal attorneys into senior Justice Department roles or lifetime
judicial nominations.

Not career prosecutors. Not independent legal minds. His personal defense
team.

And a growing number of judicial nominees share the same defining
credential: loyalty proven in Trump’s own legal battles.

Let’s be clear: these aren’t neutral appointments. They’re rewards. And
they create an obvious conflict of interest — people who defended one man
now serving in roles that demand independence from him.

That’s not how a justice system is supposed to work. The DOJ isn’t a
president’s law firm. The federal judiciary isn’t a loyalty program. But
that’s how it’s being treated.

And the result is a pipeline from “Trump’s personal lawyer” to “lifetime
federal judge” — shaping the courts around allegiance, not independence.

corruption, block the extremist nominees, and demand a judiciary that

## The Capitalist exists because of you, and we want to hear from you!
**[Become a paid subscriber today and access the Live Capitalist chat](https://substack.com/redirect/5057539d-d373-42b8-be7b-52d056c763f2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ Subscribe here now](https://substack.com/redirect/5057539d-d373-42b8-be7b-52d056c763f2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
* * *
I wonder if those who read my stuff here regularly get the impression I'm a dark person. I'm not. I'm actually pretty joyful and smiley... like most Americans. I am aware that my last few articles have been angry. I do get angry especially when things don't have to be thus.
So much of what is expensive, cumbersome, or an infringement on my rights (and yours), so much of what makes life difficult, is due to people with a self-serving agenda. We have too many people whose life entails butting into the lives of others. Leave people alone and they tend to be OK. And happy.
My work takes me to the most rural parts of the nation from the north slope of Alaska to small towns in Louisiana, and something I see in every state I've been to (46 of 50): Americans are quite happy. Yeah, they'll complain about gas prices and taxes and the rain or lack thereof, but they are very grounded, stable, kind, normal. I'd even say Americans are simple, but not "simple" as an insult.
Simple in the way a great cheeseburger is simple.
Simple in the way Beethoven's 5th is just a few notes.
Simple is good.
Watch a show on TV called "My Lottery Dream House". It's about people who won the lottery and go hunting for a dream home... you probably figured that out from the title. I marvel at what constitutes their dream. 1800 square feet in Toledo for $245,000. A split level in Chattanooga near a park. A powder room. A deck off the kitchen. A screened porch.
This is not "Lifestyles of the Rich and Famous". Champagne wishes and caviar dreams? No. Americans are simple.
I can't watch the show too often. The host is so in-your-face uncomfortably, aggressively, flamboyantly gay that it exceeds my capacity. I wonder if I should be wearing protection. It's frustrating the producers thrust so much upon us. He's probably a likable enough guy if the show weren't so desperate to turn him into a cause or a caricature. I am admittedly not tolerant. Tolerance is not a virtue, FYI, but look at me starting _a whole nother_ article...
Back to simple.
The show is an insight into how average we Americans are. Here are people who won six and seven figure sums, and they are not looking for heated driveways and limestone wine vaults. They are excited, giddy even, to own a very average home.

---|---|---
Everyone's hunting for the next Unicorn.
The type of "category disruptor" that grows fast and turns early believers into big winners.
59,000+ investors think that**[Mode Mobile](https://substack.com/redirect/57bf3ac9-89a6-46e3-b18f-8899ae567bf7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **could be one of those rare finds.
Americans spend 4 1⁄2 hours on their phones daily, and Mode Mobile is monetizing that screentime. With **[$1B+ earned by over 490M customers](https://substack.com/redirect/57bf3ac9-89a6-46e3-b18f-8899ae567bf7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and 32,481% revenue growth, Mode's EarnPhone is turning smartphones into income generating assets.
Their previous raises sold out, and the company is now offering pre-IPO shares at $0.50/share with up to 20% bonus, exclusive to early investors.
Being early is everything, and this window is still open.
**[Review the offer before it closes](https://substack.com/redirect/57bf3ac9-89a6-46e3-b18f-8899ae567bf7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ Click here](https://substack.com/redirect/57bf3ac9-89a6-46e3-b18f-8899ae567bf7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
* * *
Simple is good.
This beautiful quality in Americans is what makes the ongoing fraud investigations happening nationwide so much more egregious. It does not have to be this way, but bad people with an agenda make it so. Oh boy... here comes my angry side.
A White House official **[recently posted](https://substack.com/redirect/4bbff900-af12-4bf8-a3c1-b598927f9531?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** something online which makes one want to grab the torch and pitchfork. In one state, 14,000 people driving luxury vehicles all on government food stamps. Lamborghinis. Bentleys. Porches. Maseratis. Billions of dollars stolen every year from good Americans, under the guise of "helping the poor" when the fraud is overwhelming. The fraud offsets any good the program itself pretends to do.
Tens of billions in daycare center fraud in Minnesota and hospice fraud in California. One guy in Columbus, Ohio operates 288 Medicaid companies and bills the government for $250 million a year, and the whole thing is a fraud. The whole thing.
The total failure of government at such an offensive level makes one look into Ted Kaczynski. OK, that's a joke, but you get the point. How can our government be so criminally negligent and / or complicit? Who looked at the application and does due diligence? Who confirmed the billing and the invoices? Who wrote the checks?
And how are they not tarred and feathered at this point?
Because you and I both know that our same government comes after us with armed men if we make don't pay our taxes. I was audited once (for political reasons). It is not fun. IRS agents and their scrutiny with implications of malfeasance and allusions to criminal prosecution. And yet, that same government, is indifferent to the rampant theft.
It is the stuff of manifestos. Again, a joke. My jokes are dark.
Maybe I am dark. Maybe I am angry. Or maybe I'm just eager for justice to be served to those who use my tax dollars as their ATM. I want the same oversight of check-writing bureaucrats as the County Sheriff who watches traffic on I-81. I want Medicaid facilities to get the same routine inspection as the greasy spoon in town. I want those getting government checks to jump through the same hoops as the guy trying to put up a shed in his yard.
Man, you build a fence improperly and you got three or four inspectors with badges and clipboards coming up your driveway, but you run a fraudulent government-funded business, and no one seems to be perturbed.
I am perturbed, because this is all so very simple, and simple is good.
All this fraud does not hurt some fictional Jay Gatsby. It hurts the lottery dream house couple who thanks Jesus for an attached garage. It's the average Americans, the regular Americans, the good and kind Americans, who are being fleeced by scumbags who use "hospice" and "autistic children daycare" and "healthcare for the poor" to enrich themselves discovering those good and kind people are also gullible. You tell those great Americans the aids is for the needy, for the sick, and they'll look away, grateful, like the TV lottery winners who upgraded to a kitchen with a pantry.
It's also so preventable and yet so deliberate while the couple who I watched on a TV real estate show, squirming at the host, is thrilled to have a half-finished basement is being taxed while the Somali "refugee" on food stamps drives a Ferrari.
How could I not be angry? Guess that's why I wrote this manifesto.
That wasn't a joke.
Honor and courage.

Man, you build a fence improperly and you got three or four inspectors with badges and clipboards coming up your driveway, but you run a fraudulent government-funded business, and no one seems to be perturbed. I am perturbed, because this is all so very simple, and simple is good. All this fraud does not hurt some fictional Jay Gatsby. It hurts the lottery dream house couple who thanks Jesus for an attached garage. It's the average Americans, the regular Americans, the good and kind Americans, who are being fleeced by scumbags who use "hospice" and "autistic children daycare" and "healthcare for the poor" to enrich themselves discovering those good and kind people are also gullible. You tell those great Americans the aids is for the needy, for the sick, and they'll look away, grateful, like the TV lottery winners who upgraded to a kitchen with a pantry. It's also so preventable and yet so deliberate while the couple who I watched on a TV real estate show, squirming at the host, is thrilled to have a half-finished basement is being taxed while the Somali "refugee" on food stamps drives a Ferrari. How could I not be angry? Guess that's why I wrote this manifesto. That wasn't a joke. Honor and courage. clean_body: A historic opportunity to honor veterans| | | | Patriot, It's Gary Sinise here. You may know me from my roles in movies like Apollo 13 and The Green Mile or the CBS television series CSI: NY - but it was in 1994 playing the role of Lt. Dan in Forrest Gump that changed my life and inspired my enduring connection to our defenders, veterans, and first responders. I've served as an Honorary Grand Marshal for the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. nearly every year since American Veterans Center revived it in 2005. But I've never been more excited to serve as an Honorary Grand Marshall than I am this year - the year of America's 250th birthday. Patriot, this Memorial Day marks the first major national act of remembrance of the veterans who made the ultimate sacrifice to defend America from its enemies and ensure it has remained the Land of the Free for the last 250 years. And this year's National Memorial Day Parade will be a special edition - the biggest parade yet - where national memory meets living history as veterans from every military generation celebrate America and honor the service and sacrifice of their fallen brethren. Patriot, the National Memorial Day Parade is ENIRELY FUNDED by private contributions, including from generous patriots like you. WWII veterans were a key part of the first parade when it was revived in 2005, as they have been every year since for the last 20 years. But this may be the last year we have the opportunity to have these brave men and women with us for the parade. | | | | | | | | This year is a rare moment when living witnesses to World War II and America 's 250th birthday overlap. And no matter how much you can give to this important cause, I want to ask something additional of you. On Memorial Day - not just this momentous year of military milestones, but every year - please join me in honoring those who made the ultimate sacrifice for our freedoms. Come to the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. Visit a local veterans' cemetery. Send a note to a family of the fallen. Or simply take a quiet moment to think about the men and women who gave their lives to defend OUR country. I believe that while we can never do enough to express our gratitude to our defenders, veterans, and first responders, we can always do a little more. Patriot, thank you for your support of America 's heroes. Sincerely, Tim Holbert President American Veterans Center | | | The mission of the American Veterans Center and the World War II Veterans Committee is to preserve and promote the legacy and experiences of America's veterans and active duty service personnel from World War II through today. A non-profit educational organization, the AVC and WWIIVC are funded solely through generous contributions from people like you. All contributions are tax-deductible. subject: Why is the DNC hiding the 2024 autopsy report?
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
If we don’t have the courage to do this, how will we win over voters?
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260509-1&t=1&akid=3456%2E587540%2ENAlONL)
[](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260509_1_dnc.Dh8vJ5&refcode=em20260509-3456&t=2&akid=3456%2E587540%2ENAlONL)
Peter,
**Why is DNC Chair Ken Martin refusing to release the 2024 autopsy report?**
In an interview on Pod Save America, he told Jon Favreau that “there is no smoking gun” in the report and that it would distract us from the next election.
If we don’t have the courage to hold ourselves accountable and release an autopsy report (which Ken Martin ran his DNC campaign on releasing), how are we going to convince voters that we are offering them anything new in 2026, or 2028 for that matter?
**_How can we expect to win by doing the same thing all over again?_**
In 2024, the message voters heard from Democrats was:
We know that you’re telling us that prices are too high. We know you’re worried that the President is too old.
_But you’re wrong._ We told those voters over and over and over again, with the force of several billion dollars behind it, not to believe their eyes or their wallets.
If we can’t have the level of accountability necessary to handle the release of an autopsy report, I don’t know what there is to be said about the future of the Democratic Party. But I do know it’s not going to be productive for the American people for us to continue to run negative campaigns every cycle about what we’re _not_ — instead of who we are and what we will fight for.
**This year, Leaders We Deserve is backing a slate of bold progressives that are throwing out the old establishment playbook and running on campaigns that actually inspire voters to believe in them.** But these young candidates are facing tremendous opposition from the status quo, and _they need our support to win._

name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: Nothing will change until we do this
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
This is an anti-corruption campaign

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=2892%2E4032634%2Eg8qH64)
---
Here’s the truth: **Nothing will change until we tackle one specific problem head on: corruption.** Our government has been hijacked by the rich and powerful. It works great for defense contractors. It works great for the gun lobby. It works great for Big Pharma companies. It works great for Big Tech CEOs. It works great for billionaires. It works great for politicians who are willing to sell out to the highest bidder. We have a government that works for those at the top — and only those at the top who are looking to get richer. Our campaign finance laws enable this. Powerful special interests and billionaires use their piles of money to fund campaigns and support politicians that will block any legislation that threatens their bottom line. That was true before the Trump era. He took an already rigged system to the extreme. He is the worst symptom — not the cause — of our corrupt system. So defeating Trump just to go back to business as usual won't be enough. We need to hold him and his cronies accountable for breaking the law. Then we need to clean up the corruption in Washington to guarantee our government can never be hijacked again. **That’s what I’m focused on.** I’m putting my resources towards winning the midterms in November so that Donald Trump no longer has free reign to do anything he wants. And I’m urging the Democratic party to adopt aggressive, bold, transformational changes after we win. I have a long list of plans to root corruption out of Washington. They will impose an enforceable code of conduct on the Supreme Court, require the president and vice president to disclose and divest from any potential financial conflicts of interest, ban all individual stock ownership by members of Congress, padlock the revolving door between lobbyists and government, create a new anti-corruption agency dedicated to enforcing federal ethics laws, get Big Money out of politics, and much more. **We can only make real progress on issues impacting our country if we root out this corruption.** [**If you’re able, will you pitch in $28 or any amount to help power our anti-corruption campaign? Every donation is another signal that the American people are demanding real change and calling for a country that works for everyone, not just the rich and powerful.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3630?amount=28&t=8&akid=2892%2E4032634%2Eg8qH64)

Here in TX-03 I have watched the same playbook run in slow motion. The district was redrawn to stretch farther east and absorb five rural counties, pulling Frisco out entirely, splitting Plano, and fracturing Collin County voters across multiple districts. [**Help us fight back against this by putting someone in Congress who will introduce the Let Voters Choose Act, a bill that bans partisan gerrymandering.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt81pp880WHSCnXP9aeqZK6-sk_Nl7Gw0Jja_YmTiolmpea4004-zmW11iiHwpGYe0vJQqy-DRrlnnptm32jEW5MZRlJIzq9QXhuLLGlHCNCxEyPa14hyCePZvLn2kUFncIYaCOp6FCqxS26ogpAHMEAceV_sMkG0A0zuY6nLXvmNvcpb-HXX3l3J_s7KK0hvbfbfQvBYDUP-4zHYZ8avj2uJGWJ1bZ6ZuxId3lytVlzye46k633ZwPvs_psQ8nscV6Ifstwxm2Bi9DyJRWNGQKsKIwEBXthZ1E6iAWxqwFhC3/4qh/KqqPYAlJQHGsO6cji1pGtw/h2/h001.OM6Zd3Wtif17SXnjqxMVlc_CvAspi6nGLcq5brEWa_A) My proposed bill requires maps to be drawn only after each census by independent commissions, and prohibits the unnecessary splitting of cities and counties that belong together. Democracy is the most remarkable governing invention in human history and the one worth fighting for above all others. I know that because I spent 20 years as a combat aviator defending it. People have bled and died on every continent for the right to choose who represents them, and the Voting Rights Act of 1965 existed because Americans understood that the vote could be stolen not just through intimidation at the polls but through the architecture of the system itself. The Supreme Court has been quietly dismantling those protections for years and what we are watching in Tennessee and Texas right now is what happens when those guardrails come down. Voters should choose their representatives. **The moment politicians get to choose their voters instead, democracy becomes a performance rather than a promise.** Keith Self has said nothing about any of this because the map that stretched TX-03 eastward benefits him directly. He is the incumbent a rigged map was designed to protect. Hi friends, this is Marilyn writing. I know you're expecting Lucas to come up with something super insightful, as he does, but instead you're getting me. Don't worry, he will be back soon, meanwhile, I promise to put a lot of extra effort into this piece because it's so important right now!
I will start by saying, that as you probably know, a lot has happened in the world the last few weeks, but also in our family. We took a little break to go on an family vacation and, with 4 children, you can imagine how our hands were quite full. Right after that, Lukie turned 1 year old! Time absolutely flies--[that little one took his first few steps that same week](https://substack.com/redirect/57350ce2-1eac-40ac-b010-ceabecb397d9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
And lastly, Lucas got knee surgery done right after that. He has been in recovery, and it has been heavier on his body than he expected. He had not had surgery since he was a kid and thought he'd be back on his feet right after. Moms that have had C-sections like I did with both my kids, will understand when I say this: bless his heart. But I am very respectful of his situation, as he injured his knee while he was on active duty as a Marine. Another reason to love the VA.
But like I said before, he will be back soon, hopefully in the next week or so. Now that we've caught up, we can dive into the world outside and today's Substack issue.
Lucas's Substack is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9sdWNhc2t1bmNlLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.iS0KzdD1NGexIyeas9TYHNo56Ar1xcRTcvtwm2WNvHU?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=197016408)
**Data center fights are everywhere right now.**
If you haven't seen in the news, Utah is fighting against a massive data center that was recently approved, despite the [many residents' protest against it](https://substack.com/redirect/9a44e177-a621-4f43-9192-390d831b6237?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). And not for little reason, this Data Center's footprint is roughly **2.5 times larger than the island of Manhattan.** Bigger than [Bryce Canyon National Park](https://substack.com/redirect/2384055a-031c-4771-a034-cb0252029064?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Bigger and hungrier than most of us can even imagine.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0fe983d7-1753-4e86-a175-aba52ba62986?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_Credit:[NASA Earth](https://substack.com/redirect/f9179fb6-2b71-412f-8fe9-10b4860278b5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_
There's been a similar fight here in Independence, Missouri, where we live (right outside of Kansas City, Missouri for our non-Missourian readers) with [leaders similarly approving a new data center](https://substack.com/redirect/5e2501e6-d1d6-4359-8514-a7576feb2299?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) echoing all sorts of company promises. Like the byline on the actual tech company's website: "Nebius is a private, European-based technology company. The development _is expected to bring tens of millions of tax dollars to the City of Independence_."
According to most report, Nebius is going to pay about $30 million dollars to the City of Independence each year. [It ](https://substack.com/redirect/3bd8ab26-b693-4bc5-9e86-6070e67f9508?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[would](https://substack.com/redirect/3bd8ab26-b693-4bc5-9e86-6070e67f9508?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[ have been around $300 million per year if the city hadn't given the data center a 90% tax break during their negotiations](https://substack.com/redirect/3bd8ab26-b693-4bc5-9e86-6070e67f9508?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). But, then again, to be fair, the land currently generates just a few thousand dollars a year just sitting there, so even after the abatements it's a lot more money than was originally coming.
Which makes it sound like a win, right?
Unfortunately, one of the big problems with these negotiations is that they often focus on tax dollars and don't think about all the other costs and consequences. So, what _should_ towns across the country, like Independence, be negotiating before saying yes to AI?
This is important for everyone to know so that we can hold our leaders accountable and don't just say yes to data centers while entering into deals _we may not fully understand_. Because the reality is that despite all their promises, once a data center is built it doesn't employ the towns, it _plugs_ _into_ it.
**What 's actually being built?**
To put it simple, a modern AI data center isn't just another commercial building. It's heavy industry. More like the kind of infrastructure you'd find in places like [Louisiana's petrochemical corridor ("Cancer Alley"):](https://substack.com/redirect/693a9979-35ad-4de4-9a1b-35378150e3d7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) facilities that run constantly, draw enormous resources, and reshape the systems around them. Except instead of refining oil, these facilities refine data. And they do it at a scale that's easy to underestimate.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fa047985-7f25-4d05-9ba1-4c5362bf6911?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_Louisiana "Cancer Alley" petrochemical corridor. Credit: Gerald Herbert/AP Photo_
The Nebius plant in Independence, for example, is projected to use the same amount of electricity as 400,000 Independence homes would. Note: there are only 50,000 households in all of Independence... That's a pretty big change.
The largest new AI projects go even further. Some proposed clusters, like OpenAI's, are expected to consume [as much power as](https://substack.com/redirect/57b16a63-9f6a-4884-b47c-45e5ba25089e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) _[New York City and San Diego combined](https://substack.com/redirect/57b16a63-9f6a-4884-b47c-45e5ba25089e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/57b16a63-9f6a-4884-b47c-45e5ba25089e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[during peak demand](https://substack.com/redirect/57b16a63-9f6a-4884-b47c-45e5ba25089e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_. To quote some writers and experts, "**it is scary** ".
Basically, these data centers add a large city's worth of energy demand to much smaller towns. And this is not a slow shift. It's an explosion that sends electricity prices through the roof for everyday people.
Bloomberg analyzed electricity price increases in regions located near significant data centers and found that electricity per month costs as much as [267% more](https://substack.com/redirect/6d576e99-2a6f-4ab9-a7a7-5e7cd86f49e5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) than it did just five years ago.
Let's do some back of the napkin math for Independence to see just how quickly the promised $30 million a year in tax revenue evaporates and then goes very, very negative for the people of Independence.
With 50,000 Independence households spending about $150 per month in electricity bills, we're talking about $90 million per year in total household electric bills. If the Independence electricity rate goes up _just 33%_ because of that massive data center, which it certainly will, then the $30 million per year in revenue is already zeroed out.
Anything after that, and the people of Independence simply have less money than they did before the center came. When the price of electricity doubles, which is highly likely based on the Bloomberg data, the people of Independence will be paying $90 million more in electricity than they were before the data center arrived, and only getting $30 million in exchange.
The math ain't mathin, it is absolutely brutal.
Anywhere you live in the Midwest, an equally bad deal is coming for you, too.
Big AI is targeting places like Missouri, Kansas, Iowa, and Indiana. Not by accident, but because the Midwest has cheap land, a willingness to generate power, cash-strapped local governments, and water.
**So what about water?**
Data centers [run on water as much as they run on electricity](https://substack.com/redirect/53cc5b04-a3f3-4f8e-9a92-94ffa220e833?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Servers generate heat. To prevent overheating, many facilities rely on evaporative cooling systems, which consume outstandingly large volumes of water every day.
We're talking about a demand that eventually require [hundreds of millions to over a ](https://substack.com/redirect/1c4a5b6b-c35c-46b9-9922-ff5cdd5f3e0b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[billion gallons of water](https://substack.com/redirect/1c4a5b6b-c35c-46b9-9922-ff5cdd5f3e0b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[per day](https://substack.com/redirect/1c4a5b6b-c35c-46b9-9922-ff5cdd5f3e0b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/1c4a5b6b-c35c-46b9-9922-ff5cdd5f3e0b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[nationally](https://substack.com/redirect/1c4a5b6b-c35c-46b9-9922-ff5cdd5f3e0b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), placing significant strain on local systems, especially the smaller municipalities that these data centers target.
Water systems in the US are highly fragmented, with more than 50,000 separate systems around the country. Most Midwestern communities rely on these small independent water systems that were never designed for large industrial-scale continuous demand.
And something we rarely hear about when talking about water consumption in Data Centers, is that after the water has been used in them, a large portion of the water used _doesn 't_ come back in a form communities can easily reuse.
Part of it evaporates into the air as part of the cooling process, meaning it doesn't return into the local water system, _it is effectively removed from the watershed_.
The remaining water, known as "[blowdown](https://substack.com/redirect/af840141-5b32-442c-952f-cd40e7279a1d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" is discharged as wastewater.
This wastewater contains concentrated minerals and treatment chemicals that often require additional processing before it can safely re-enter municipal systems.
That means that when a data center comes in, the question isn't just "do we have water?" It's: can our system handle sustained high-volume withdrawals all year round? What about on hot summer days when data centers use 30 times as much as their daily average? Or in a drought year? And, most importantly, what infrastructure do we need to add to make it that way and who is going to pay for it?
No one knows how much extra the people of Independence are going to pay on their water bills, in addition to their higher electric bill, because nobody properly looked into it.
The only thing for certain, is that we are essentially paying the data center to come here and suck wealth out of our community for almost nothing in return.
Because unlike factories or other large employers, despite demanding major infrastructure support, Data Centers create relatively few permanent jobs.
**Will these Data Centers bring many jobs to the town that hosts them?**
This is usually the first thing people hear: jobs.
It is the reason many communities say yes.
And at first, they do, actually.
Building a data center takes hundreds, sometimes thousands of workers. There are contractors, electricians, engineers, and suppliers. Local hotels fill up. Restaurants get busy.
It feels like growth.
But it's short-lived.
Once the facility is built, the number of permanent jobs drops sharply. A large data center can operate with _dozens of employees_ , not hundreds. Many roles are highly specialized. Many systems are automated.
Ironically, the companies and communities [pouring billions into AI](https://substack.com/redirect/94ee1ca3-89c3-4417-84e3-d8dd7d8d0f51?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) are actually [reducing their workforces](https://substack.com/redirect/af065a23-3d4e-47cf-84cb-10642bffdbfb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and their efforts are likely reduce overall jobs in the long run.
[Over 100,000 workers were impacted by AI-related layoffs in 2025. Over 70k more in these first months of 2026. More than 45 CEOs have explicitly cited AI as a reason for cutting jobs.](https://substack.com/redirect/07cae29f-7945-4880-989b-ef2d6ea4079d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
So I guess I was wrong when I said we are just paying them to come in and suck wealth out of our community. We are also essentially paying them to come in and destroy jobs!
**What 's Already Changing and What Still Needs to Be Asked**
Fortunately, some people are beginning to realize these are not ordinary developments and that they shouldn't be treated that way.
Just last month, for example, Independence voters ousted [everyone on the municipal ballot who had forced through the data center approval](https://substack.com/redirect/b254a172-aedd-4cab-af59-ceede07aca26?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)!
[Kansas City recently passed one of its first major zoning changes specifically targeting data centers](https://substack.com/redirect/c73f2d07-21ad-46fb-8bbd-ff74b047b068?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), limiting where they can be built and requiring more public review.
And in Peculiar and St. Charles, Missouri, residents actually stopped the data centers from coming in at all
But, so far, it's hard to see any concrete examples of communities setting the right terms for these companies before they arrive. It's been a bit of an all or nothing approach. And community leaders are still often only asking "home much revenue will this bring in" without also asking "how much is this going to cost our citizens."
I wanted to share all of this information with you today because I believe that can change if we all know what's actually happening and what we are up against and can educate our leaders. So that instead of accepting the terms from these companies, we start setting them.
So, as always, please share this with anyone who is thinking about or could be impacted by a data center, thank you for reading, and keep on fighting!
Marilyn Kunce
*On a different note, truly there are a lot of news coming at us at once these days, it is hard to pick a topic when so much is going on around the world. We are hoping to write more about some of these pieces of policy that are being rolled back and bring very bad consequences for everyone. Lucas and I have each very different areas that we personally focus our work on, which makes it great for bringing you loads of great insights.
Some ideas I have, personally, are regarding the environmental rollbacks, let me know in the comments if you'd like me to write a piece for each? Or if you'd prefer if I grouped them on themes? Or if you want a list with the big picture points and what to look for? I want to be able to dive hard on the policies, the consequences, what it means for the Midwest and our family's health and future. Should I do a podcast on these? Truly, I have so much to tell you all, that I am really thinking about putting a podcast out every other week with the major rollbacks in simple words. Let me know what you guys want, and I will do my best! I also have the honor to work with some people who are absolute experts on certain topics, and I am more than happy to talk to them, and break it down to simple words.

Hello friends,
We're excited to invite you to a Suozzi for Congress Primary Canvass Launch on Saturday, May 16th at 10:30am! We'd love to have you there, whether you've volunteered with us before or this is your first time getting involved.

RSVP through Mobilize: https://www.mobilize.us/suozziforcongress/event/951996/_Feel free to RSVP our team via email - madsionforman05@gmail.com or aidands2026@gmail.com_

If you've been looking for a way to get involved, this is the perfect place to start. We hope to see you Saturday!

body:
Team Pappas is reaching out to our most engaged supporters to take part in our 2026 NH Strategy Focus Group – and we’re hoping you’ll be one of them.
# [](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1&akid=6553%2E582294%2E3-b20T)

| Letter from the Chair
---
Tyranny of the Minority - And the Wisdom of Balance
Dear Nebraska Republicans,
Our Founding Fathers were brilliant. They designed the United States Constitution with a clear purpose: to protect the American people from two deadly threats--tyranny of the majority and tyranny of the minority.
Tyranny of the Majority occurs when a passionate mob or numerical majority tramples the rights, traditions, and freedoms of smaller groups or individuals. The Founders feared this deeply, knowing pure (direct) democracy could lead to mob rule, property seizures, or the oppression of dissenting voices. They countered it with safeguards like the Bill of Rights, the Senate's equal state representation, the Electoral College, and a republic structured to refine and filter raw majority will.
Tyranny of the Minority, by contrast, arises when a small, determined clique--through courts, procedures, or amplified influence--imposes its agenda against the clear wishes of the broader population. This is ruled by obstruction rather than consent.
The genius of the American system lies in its deliberate balance: majority rule tempered by minority protections, and minority rights shielded without granting veto power over the common good. The three branches of government--Legislative, Executive, and Judicial--along with federalism and checks and balances, were engineered to navigate between these twin dangers.
That system has served America well for nearly 250 years. But today, radical activists, activist judges, and fringe voices are exploiting procedural loopholes to impose their agenda on the silent majority. This is tyranny of the minority--and it is happening at the federal level, in Nebraska state government, and even at the organizational level of the Nebraska Republican Party.
Federal Government: Where the Minority Rules
Too often in Washington, a handful of voices override the will of millions:

* Activist Judges: Unelected federal judges routinely block the policies of duly elected Republican presidents and Congresses. One or two judges can halt energy projects, border security measures, or election integrity laws that the American people overwhelmingly support.

* Senatorial Filibuster (Cloture Rule): The 60-vote threshold allows a minority of 41 senators to kill legislation supported by the majority.
* Race-Based Gerrymandering: Recently overturned by the Supreme Courts, some states have drawn districts with race as the primary factor, denying fair representation even where conservative voters form the clear majority.

* We also see the emergence of public opinion surveys being touted as legitimate "polling" to skew legislators' views on issues by misrepresenting the will of the majority.

These tactics let a vocal minority dictate terms to the hardworking majority.
Challenges Closer to Home in Nebraska

* Unicameral Cloture Motion: In our one-house legislature, it takes 33 votes to end debate and pass a bill. A minority of just 17 senators can block the will of the other 32. Nebraska voters keep electing strong Republican majorities--yet minority procedural hurdles keep conservative priorities bottled up.

* Inside the Nebraska Republican Party: Small fringe groups--often with limited actual support--use social media to amplify their voices far beyond their numbers. A handful of disgruntled accounts can dominate conversations and divert attention of leaders from bigger issues.

This distorts our Party's direction and drowns out the reasonable, majority view of Nebraska conservatives who simply want lower taxes, secure borders, and pro-life policies.
A Call to Harmony and Balance
The Founders did not choose between majority rule and minority rights--they sought harmony between them. True republican government thrives when the majority governs with wisdom and restraint, while minorities retain strong protections for their God-given rights.
Let us recommit to that vision. By rejecting both mob rule and minority obstructionism, we can restore a government that truly reflects the will of Nebraska's citizens and America's hardworking families. Together, through principled leadership and civic engagement, we can build a stronger, more united future--one rooted in liberty, fairness, and the timeless promise of e pluribus unum: out of many, one.
In Liberty and in Truth, Mary Jane Truemper Chairman, Nebraska Republican Party

clean_body: News, events, and action items to keep Nebraska red and growing strong. | | | | | | Letter from the Chair Tyranny of the Minority - And the Wisdom of Balance Dear Nebraska Republicans, Our Founding Fathers were brilliant. They designed the United States Constitution with a clear purpose: to protect the American people from two deadly threats--tyranny of the majority and tyranny of the minority. Tyranny of the Majority occurs when a passionate mob or numerical majority tramples the rights, traditions, and freedoms of smaller groups or individuals. The Founders feared this deeply, knowing pure (direct) democracy could lead to mob rule, property seizures, or the oppression of dissenting voices. They countered it with safeguards like the Bill of Rights, the Senate's equal state representation, the Electoral College, and a republic structured to refine and filter raw majority will. Tyranny of the Minority, by contrast, arises when a small, determined clique--through courts, procedures, or amplified influence--imposes its agenda against the clear wishes of the broader population. This is ruled by obstruction rather than consent. The genius of the American system lies in its deliberate balance: majority rule tempered by minority protections, and minority rights shielded without granting veto power over the common good. The three branches of government--Legislative, Executive, and Judicial--along with federalism and checks and balances, were engineered to navigate between these twin dangers. That system has served America well for nearly 250 years. But today, radical activists, activist judges, and fringe voices are exploiting procedural loopholes to impose their agenda on the silent majority. This is tyranny of the minority--and it is happening at the federal level, in Nebraska state government, and even at the organizational level of the Nebraska Republican Party. Federal Government: Where the Minority Rules Too often in Washington, a handful of voices override the will of millions: Activist Judges: Unelected federal judges routinely block the policies of duly elected Republican presidents and Congresses. One or two judges can halt energy projects, border security measures, or election integrity laws that the American people overwhelmingly support. Senatorial Filibuster (Cloture Rule): The 60-vote threshold allows a minority of 41 senators to kill legislation supported by the majority. Race-Based Gerrymandering: Recently overturned by the Supreme Courts, some states have drawn districts with race as the primary factor, denying fair representation even where conservative voters form the clear majority. We also see the emergence of public opinion surveys being touted as legitimate "polling" to skew legislators' views on issues by misrepresenting the will of the majority. These tactics let a vocal minority dictate terms to the hardworking majority. Challenges Closer to Home in Nebraska Unicameral Cloture Motion: In our one-house legislature, it takes 33 votes to end debate and pass a bill. A minority of just 17 senators can block the will of the other 32. Nebraska voters keep electing strong Republican majorities--yet minority procedural hurdles keep conservative priorities bottled up. Inside the Nebraska Republican Party: Small fringe groups--often with limited actual support--use social media to amplify their voices far beyond their numbers. A handful of disgruntled accounts can dominate conversations and divert attention of leaders from bigger issues. This distorts our Party's direction and drowns out the reasonable, majority view of Nebraska conservatives who simply want lower taxes, secure borders, and pro-life policies. A Call to Harmony and Balance The Founders did not choose between majority rule and minority rights--they sought harmony between them. True republican government thrives when the majority governs with wisdom and restraint, while minorities retain strong protections for their God-given rights. Let us recommit to that vision. By rejecting both mob rule and minority obstructionism, we can restore a government that truly reflects the will of Nebraska's citizens and America's hardworking families. Together, through principled leadership and civic engagement, we can build a stronger, more united future--one rooted in liberty, fairness, and the timeless promise of e pluribus unum: out of many, one. Yesterday was a reminder that powerful people will always try to protect power, even when it comes at the expense of voters and our democracy.
They will use every threat and trick. By overturning the new maps and the will of Virginia voters, the Virginia Supreme Court joins those who have capitulated when they had their chance to put our country and Constitution first.
That is the job of historians. My job is urgent and clear – I am going to defeat Rep. John McGuire and flip Virginia’s Fifth District. I am the only Democrat to win this district in a generation, and I am going to do it again this year, with your help. These midterms are game over or game on for our Constitution and system of checks and balances.
The people of Central and Southside Virginia cannot afford two more years of this chaos, corruption, and cruelty from Washington. Our food banks are bursting at the seams from historic levels of hunger, because of SNAP cuts and food prices. Emergency rooms are overflowing because of Medicaid cuts and premium hikes. Folks do not expect Washington to solve every problem, but they do expect their elected representatives, like McGuire, not to make their lives worse.
Our region deserves real representation. In listening sessions across our region, people on the right, left, and center agree on one thing – McGuire needs to be fired. He could have chosen to fight for our communities, but McGuire chose instead to duck and cover. He has voted to take more money out of our pockets, and refused to answer to constituents who ask him why.
Folks across Central and Southside Virginia know that I am a fighter. That I listen. And that my priority will be immediate economic relief for families across our communities. From expanding affordable healthcare to repairing the Robertson Bridge, I will focus on what brings down costs, pushes up paychecks, and forces the powerful to play by the same set of rules as the rest of us.
We are going to win this seat back for the people. I am the only Democrat in a generation to win a congressional race in Virginia's Fifth District, when I flipped the seat in 2008 against a six-term Republican incumbent.
Since launching my campaign, I have been in every corner of this district. I’ve traveled to all 72 counties in Wisconsin multiple times, and this is what I hear over and over...

Every Wisconsinite, rural or urban, is sick and tired of the special treatment that the top 1% receives, while they struggle to keep their lights on and bills paid.

# [#]
For six decades, the Voting Rights Act has stood as one of the most important protections in our democracy by preventing racial gerrymandering, voter suppression, and efforts to dilute the political power of Black Americans and other minority communities.

But Trump’s Supreme Court has turned back the clock on voting rights and the racial justice movement.

By significantly weakening the Voting Rights Act, the Court has opened the door for Republican states to draw maps that reduce the voting power and representation of minority communities.

This is exactly what MAGA wanted: the White House, Congress, and the Supreme Court to undo the progress and reforms of the last 60 years. Sadly, this court is more focused on power and loyalty to Donald Trump than impartial justice.

As your representative, I will fight to restore the full promise of the Voting Rights Act and defend every American’s right to have an equal voice in our democracy. It is a foundational promise that America must uphold.

If you’re with me, I’m asking you to sign on to protect and expand voting rights. [https://secure.ngpvan.com/g3YhSQjaQkSLvM87_-a-GQ2]

body:
At least one of our opponents has a history of working for billionaires and taking money from oil lobbyists, the banking industry, and DTE energy.
#
Peter,
**We just learned that we will have not one, but two opponents in our Democratic primary.** But with neither having filed a required fundraising report with the Federal Election Commission, it leads us to ask, **who is funding them?**
**At least one of our opponents has a history of working for billionaires and corporate polluters while accepting money from oil lobbyists, the banking industry, and DTE Energy.**
Voters deserve a voice in Congress who will always put their interests ahead of Big Money and the billionaire bullies. And that’s what I’ve done throughout my career fighting for you.
**In the past, people have been offered tens of millions of dollars to run against me. With just over three months until Election Day, I need your urgent support right now.**

Patriot,
---
It's Gary Sinise here. You may know me from my roles in movies like Apollo 13 _ _ and The Green Mile or the CBS television series CSI: NY - but it was in 1994 playing the role of Lt. Dan in Forrest Gump that changed my life and inspired my enduring connection to our defenders, veterans, and first responders. I've served as an Honorary Grand Marshal for the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. nearly every year since American Veterans Center revived it in 2005. **But I've never been more excited to serve as an Honorary Grand Marshall than I am this year - the year of America's 250****th**** birthday.**
---

Patriot, this Memorial Day marks the first major national act of remembrance of the veterans who made the ultimate sacrifice to defend America from its enemies and ensure it has remained the Land of the Free for the last 250 years. And this year's National Memorial Day Parade will be a special edition - the biggest parade yet - where national memory meets living history as veterans from every military generation celebrate America and honor the service and sacrifice of their fallen brethren. **Patriot, the National Memorial Day Parade is ENIRELY FUNDED by private contributions, including from generous patriots like you.** **[In light of America’s 250th birthday and the special opportunity we have to honor veterans this year, will you chip in today to help support the parade with a gift of $25, $50, $75, $150, or more?](http://links.g4yamerica.com/u/click?_t=cc7dda5c2cc64061900678c88bd3a18a&_m=e07b8283e37f44128ce1b3f0e37c598b&_e=tOgCWpNrkNCzI6oiGrNwJ7D7FqhEZc1iOWfD9h5UhdX9APkvgSLsGVkqu4rGLgnE60odeRR6SfnpDux9LVkf98OXWlwT7qCprTq78P-KI4E7UolAevoNx5OxO1EU5IG3v4QyykEjnhQh65GyYodUhNVEhDlo2Fxa202uwDjOjjGyZbHg1YmpGtL9auj1wQOyy5B9n6EVxUsP_qJAt2hZjqFxY1uogeA2hWoOpENTQxbEGtAf5ekaTOMh2izZqKFxhkvGgfqiLnh36tHKXKFZ5XhjaS2s2HcmhNLx40pRH1vPLUREll-EI3SE5FQuSkSJn0TQABJk-bhkwPk0LdIqtBpRFMIbJAcOv1mhWFvx43r_U3V6pW5M67wu-cVnoAwfZVb7XEsDpGAbw0BgBTC-ZLnAiQ650DaTOSrKroclRVpHrHZewqIiXc5d-wAPJWeZW49zPh932mDDEf6W7v5XIcwfr4M0Obl1ipf38xyil554poSP1gjMzCc1W-uo7b8NCHdsDF0shareZxxxVdspiTHFfCIxPxmDmUm9ho605jH4ci5mdI-0rDKYp9Ox60nuRl5sjkUXJ73hJL5B0ULoI4HjbPX-2Qm-KHZSnexAjK8ZakWoSVCpN4ciKlzm-Ff4vxycA-XxIzmX_vCS-aGx7UAmkiEZpLJwgv8ceCk8aBpxkonPKuHGVGEi2uOTZwLmvDNjTlYBdxf_N6QNAqSIeg%3D%3D)**

clean_body: A historic opportunity to honor veterans| | | | Patriot, It's Gary Sinise here. You may know me from my roles in movies like Apollo 13 and The Green Mile or the CBS television series CSI: NY - but it was in 1994 playing the role of Lt. Dan in Forrest Gump that changed my life and inspired my enduring connection to our defenders, veterans, and first responders. I've served as an Honorary Grand Marshal for the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. nearly every year since American Veterans Center revived it in 2005. But I've never been more excited to serve as an Honorary Grand Marshall than I am this year - the year of America's 250th birthday. Patriot, this Memorial Day marks the first major national act of remembrance of the veterans who made the ultimate sacrifice to defend America from its enemies and ensure it has remained the Land of the Free for the last 250 years. And this year's National Memorial Day Parade will be a special edition - the biggest parade yet - where national memory meets living history as veterans from every military generation celebrate America and honor the service and sacrifice of their fallen brethren. Patriot, the National Memorial Day Parade is ENIRELY FUNDED by private contributions, including from generous patriots like you. WWII veterans were a key part of the first parade when it was revived in 2005, as they have been every year since for the last 20 years. But this may be the last year we have the opportunity to have these brave men and women with us for the parade. | | | | | | | | This year is a rare moment when living witnesses to World War II and America 's 250th birthday overlap. And no matter how much you can give to this important cause, I want to ask something additional of you. On Memorial Day - not just this momentous year of military milestones, but every year - please join me in honoring those who made the ultimate sacrifice for our freedoms. Come to the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. Visit a local veterans' cemetery. Send a note to a family of the fallen. Or simply take a quiet moment to think about the men and women who gave their lives to defend OUR country. I believe that while we can never do enough to express our gratitude to our defenders, veterans, and first responders, we can always do a little more. Patriot, thank you for your support of America 's heroes.
