Democracy in America has collapsed under the weight under a corporate two-party duopoly that California has a unique and rare chance to reject by electing Butch Ware as our next Governor. | | | May 9 | | | | | | | | | | | | Readers of my column will find no surprise in the depth of the disdain I harbor for the Democratic Party. Having been thoroughly corrupted by capital and co-opted by militarism, it plays the same role with respect to the overtly fascist Republican Party that the did for the before the team closed down in 2015. Californians...enjoy a rare and unique opportunity over the next month to strike a crucial blow against the corporate two-party duopoly For those who might not have witnessed the truly delightful spectacle of a Globetrotters-Generals game, Wikipedia the Generals as "effectively being stooges for the Globetrotters," who would routinely make their hapless counterparts appear confused and out of their league by, in some cases, literally running circles around them. Democrats the same opportunity to Republicans. Many Americans are fed up with the recurring complicity of elected Democrats, but most grassroots voices can do only so much to shrug off the yolk of a supposed opposition party that plays the role of fascist . Californians, however, enjoy a rare and unique opportunity over the next month to strike a crucial blow against the corporate two-party duopoly by supporting the historic--and potentially transformative--candidacy of Green Party nominee . | | ---|---|--- Photo courtesy of UC-Santa Barbara, where Dr. Ware teaches history Thanks for reading Chronicles of a Dying Empire!You can play a key role in challenging bipartisan corruption by sharing this post--especially with anyone you know who lives in California. Democrats do not deserve support The co-optation of the Democratic Party is nothing new. I've of my life to confronting it directly, and written any number of articles exploring and it to more casual observers. The party's leaders in the Senate have Trump's most enduring actions, including , as well as the expansion of ICE into an unaccountable federal paramilitary goon squad used to suppress dissent and innocent people with impunity in broad daylight. Despite the party's consistent reliance on support from communities of color, its longtime leader in the House unapologetically on white supremacy to insulate herself from electoral accountability the one time she faced a threat in a November election, while ducking public debates and conservative policy priorities--including ironclad support for Israel, Wall Street, and the Pentagon--for nearly 40 years. As I on this platform just the other day: The Democratic Party defends the same interests as Republicans. They're not opposition. They're enablers. No one outraged by the fascism that has grown all-too-apparent in the U.S. over the past decade (after in the shadows for long before that) is going to find a solution in the Democratic Party. America desperately needs new voices Recognizing the bizarre of Washington, and the gerontocracy that has entrenched itself despite its recurring and ongoing failures, many observers have supported structural solutions, such as term limits. But, as I've , forcing turnover in the cast of characters in no way changes the play--it just changes the particular faces and personalities chosen to continue perpetrating the same fraud on well-meaning people who don't know where to turn for alternatives. But we have alternatives, and none are better poised--or prepared--than Butch Ware. An academic-artist-activist-athlete-organizer I'll admit from the outset that one reason I'm so excited about Ware's campaign is that we seem to be cut from remarkably similar cloth. I've been described as a man based on the diversity among my various pursuits, and I have yet to encounter anyone else who happened to choose such precisely identical pathways for expression and resistance. Butch is a hip-hop MC, historian, professor, prolific public speaker, direct action organizer, professional athlete, and candidate for public office. To be fair, he's more accomplished in each of those arenas than I ever will, which is among the reasons I'd be excited to see him leading our state. To his credit, Butch also seems refreshingly humble, describing in his own words as if his combination of talents and achievements fell into his lap: I got to become an emcee and a professional baseball player and still finish a PhD.... I became a PhD because I found out in school that I was better at school than I was at baseball. But before that, it was all sports for me. So, long story short....I was teaching at the University of Michigan at the time. I looked for a place to stay in shape, and I ended up getting recruited for a team in the French Elite League, and as a 40-year-old, I took the team...to the championship..... Beyond his tremendous life story and the diverse array of communities to which he has contributed, Butch also proposes a that would make an immense difference in the lives of working class Californians. The vision of that Butch Ware proposes goes to the heart of economic disparities and the affordability crisis. For instance, he has proposed plans to by supporting vacancy taxes, social housing, and rent control. Butch also proposes universal, through a plan that would end the racket of corporate health insurance and make care free at the point of use for every Californian. Butch also supports labor to a greater extent than any Democrat. He supports a statewide $25/hr minimum wage, as well as a California Public Bank poised to put the state's resources to work for workers across California. He also wants to establish a publicly owned energy grid built by union workers. His plans go beyond distributive justice to also include dramatic protections for civil rights and civil liberties. For instance, Butch wants to Make California for immigrants by closing ICE detention facilities relying on state contracts, and ending state cooperation by state authorities with federal immigration enforcement. Butch also wants to end the era of mass incarceration, by releasing incarcerated people who remain locked up for "crimes" that are no longer illegal, and building a crisis response system based on care, rather than policing. Perhaps most radically, Butch aims to of state-held lands to indigenous communities from which they were taken, and create the nation's first Reparations Task Force to provide cash reparations to repair multi-generational harm from slavery. His platform reaches principles and communities beyond those embraced by Democrats, who tend to quibble at the margins while conceding the underlying legitimacy of right wing policies. Butch envisions a different approach not only to governing, but also the process of campaigning for public office. For instance, he has gone far beyond how most political campaigns engage the public by compiling a statewide . Democrats know they can 't win a debate--and close ranks to exclude other candidates When I was publicly through a racist character assassination three months before the 2020 general election, it was because the Democratic Party establishment couldn't letting me appear on a debate stage against my opponent in the then-upcoming 2020 general election. And with good reason: Pelosi's record has long been indefensible, and I was both well-informed and fearless. Democratic strategists had watched Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez Pelosi's former lieutenant, Joe Crowley, just one election cycle earlier--particularly in a televised when she exposed his inability & unwillingness to represent the people of Queens, NY. What the learned was that they can't let voters see their alternatives. That's way Democrats have denied Ware a chance to debate the other gubernatorial candidates, while also conspiring to keep him off the ballot by inventing a series of bizarre ballot restrictions and then moving the proverbial goalposts repeatedly. Chronicles of a Dying Empire is a publication made possible by readers who appreciate independent voices. To receive new posts,sign up for a free subscription! To enable me to write more consistently, please consider becoming a paid subscriber. Only political cowards duck debates A planned debate in March at USC was mere hours before it was scheduled, due to criticism that it excluded every candidate of color--including Black, Latino, and Asian candidates--in the crowded field. The party responded by organizing forum last month featuring eight candidates, including two Latino candidates while still excluding the Black and Asian candidates. According to recent polls, Ware has statewide support than of those who were included. Notably, most polls the candidates excluded from the forum, who together have more support than any of those who were included. Responding creatively, the Ware campaign organized a , and has powerfully exposed the corruption of Democrats on . Hypocritically restricting ballot access Ballot access is perhaps the most direct--and hypocritical--way that Democrats disrespect voters. Democrats have fairly criticized the Supreme Court for reviving the Jim Crow era through its recent across the country, while at the same time working to block voters in California from even seeing their choices. This week, Californians received our ballots by mail. But one of the leading candidates for Governor--the only Black candidate with statewide support--doesn't appear on the ballot. California requires gubernatorial candidates to submit five years of tax returns. Ware complied with the requirement, only to be arbitrarily disqualified by the Secretary of State--a Democrat, acting as a loyal partisan to protect his party from electoral accountability. When Ware challenged his disqualification in court, he encountered a pattern similar to what I discovered when I sought redress for corporate newspapers with reckless disregard for the truth, in violation of . Both of us have confronted arbitrary decisions by lower court judges who have simply ignored clear legal requirements in order to protect the political establishment. As Butch has publicly: [T]hey had the full copy of both tax returns, and they admitted it in court. And their argument was, they said, "It's not our job to collate the candidates' tax returns." So they admitted that they had it in their possession, and the judge, unmoved by the fact that we had complied--they had everything they needed; we submitted it on time and they had it all; despite the moving goalposts, we complied--he said, "We're denying your writ." And he literally read out a prewritten order. The fix was in before he ever got in the court.... Overdue accountability indicates opportunism more than solidarity the strategy of Democrats at the national level in 2020, California Democratic Party Chair Rusty Hicks has publicly that candidates running under that party's banner should drop out of the race in order to consolidate support for the frontrunners, specifically in order to maintain the party's effective monopoly on state politics. Former Rep. Eric Swalwell (D-CA) was the frontrunner in the race for several months, until recent accusations of sexual assault him out of both the race and Congress. It is telling that Democrats and labor unions had Swalwell for many years, even though his misconduct had been known. Would they have supported accountability for Swalwell's known--and ignored--behavior absent fears of the Democratic field being so crowded that Republicans would take the top two positions in the primary? Having been when I ran for office by of behavior far less disturbing than the serious crimes that Swalwell appears to have actually committed, the opportunism--and by Democrats has grown hard for me to overlook. Its major cities include the country's cultural capital (Los Angeles), as well as its former counter-cultural capital and current epicenter of the technology sector (the San Francisco Bay Area) that increasingly drives the national economy. Many Americans forget that California used to be before Washington secured it through conquest. I filed to run for re-election this week because there is more we can accomplish for Northwest Washington. Some of my top priorities for next term include:
* **Addressing affordability and lowering costs:** Prices are far too high, harming the pocketbooks of working families, and I will work to bring down costs. We need reinvestments in career and technical education and training so that our students and workers are trained for good, family-supporting careers like those in aviation, manufacturing, and engineering.
* **Lowering prescription drug prices and ensuring access to health care:** I believe health care is a right, and I support universal coverage, but even with good insurance, the costs are high. For years, drug companies have tried to block competitive pricing. I helped pass landmark legislation that allows Medicare to negotiate prescription drug prices, caps out-of-pocket drug costs for seniors, and caps insulin copays at $35 per month, all while cutting the deficit by $300 billion.
* **Hold ICE accountable:** President Trump's immigration enforcement agenda has harmed families and children here in Northwest Washington and across our country.ICE must follow the same standards as other local and state law enforcement agencies. I am fighting for reforms to the Department of Homeland Security.
* **Supporting our veterans:** Northwest Washington is home to 47,000 veterans, which is 7.6 percent of the district's population. From my first days in office, I have made working with the veterans of Northwest Washington a top priority for my office. Together, we have made great progress in improving access to services for our veterans, but I know there is more work to be done. I am focused on making sure veterans have access to high-quality, timely health care, affordable housing, educational opportunities, and fulfilling employment.

These issues, along with many others like protecting our democracy, tackling the climate crisis, and getting fentanyl off our streets, are issues that make a real, tangible difference for you and your families.

Welcome to Maggie Hassan's Substack
Don't recognize this sender? [Unsubscribe with one click](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9tYWdnaWVoYXNzYW4uc3Vic3RhY2suY29tL2FjdGlvbi9kaXNhYmxlX2VtYWlsL2Rpc2FibGU_.Y3hVDcSz_wa5j4jxLQqbdWpwn-i-AJlhG5kwHsNnZP8?)

To set up your profile and discover more on Substack, [click here](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/37c0b79b-a95d-4444-9aaf-fb5b2f79ff1a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Hello, this is Senator Maggie Hassan -- and welcome to my first Substack post. Given the state of the country, I'm trying to reach as many people as I can, which is why I'll be posting here from time to time.
It's impossible to overstate the damage that Donald Trump and the Republican majorities have done to our country; unraveling hard-fought progress as they strip away health care access for everyday Americans, defund food assistance for children and families, and make it harder for seniors and people with disabilities to get the essential care that they need.
As if that isn't bad enough, this inept, careless, and corrupt majority has flouted the rule of law and the example of professional law enforcement by unleashing undisciplined and untrained ICE agents on our communities and our way of life -- all to meet arbitrary and extreme deportation quotas. Meanwhile, Americans are facing a cost-of-living crisis while the Trump family and its billionaire allies rake in more and more money for themselves.
And even worse, Donald Trump has launched a war of choice without the support of the American people, coordination with our allies, or a strategy.
Americans are experiencing something I never thought we would -- a group of so-called leaders who don't believe that they are accountable to the American people. Government of, by, and for the people has been replaced by a group of grifters and extremists who have two goals: impose an unpopular and extreme agenda on the country and enrich themselves in the process. So it's up to us to fight for freedom.
### **In New Hampshire, we 're known for our state motto, "Live Free or Die."**
We take our individual liberties seriously and know that we can never be complacent about protecting them. Fighting for freedom is an all-hands-on-deck kind of thing. It's why we insisted on pulling the presidential nominating process out of convention back rooms and into the hands of the people as we became the First in the Nation state. It's why we hold elections for state office every two years. And it's why we don't wait for other people to step forward to solve a problem or meet a need.
People in New Hampshire know that when they get involved in their communities and advocate _unapologetically_ for what they believe in, they can affect change.
My election in 2016 is an example of just that. It was a neck-and-neck race against my Republican opponent, but ultimately, I was elected to the U.S. Senate by a razor-thin margin of 1,017 votes. Months later, the Trump administration attempted to gut the Affordable Care Act, and my one vote was the margin that saved health care for millions of Americans. That's the difference an election can make -- the difference that comes when we organize, advocate, and vote.
### **Which brings me to this year 's midterm elections: an all-hands-on-deck moment if there ever was one.**
This is our opportunity to reclaim our House and Senate majorities so we can take power away from the Republican extremists and careless charlatans who are devastating our country and democracy. And it's a critical opportunity to put a necessary check on Donald Trump's power before he wreaks even more havoc over the next two years.
From New Hampshire to Georgia to Maine to Ohio to Texas, Democrats are fighting tooth and nail to take back our majority. Trump and his super PACs have already raised over $300 million this election cycle to defeat our Democratic candidates -- but I believe that our grassroots movement of freedom-loving patriots is up to the challenge.
I'm committed to supporting Democrats who are running in battleground races across the country, so that we can take back the Senate and rebuild our country.
So I'll be reaching out here to keep you up-to-date on the fight that we are waging -- right now in the Senate, on the ground in New Hampshire, and with highlights from critical races across the country. Sometimes I'll just share what's on my mind.
[And if you find my posts interesting or the races I describe compelling, and you're one of the grassroots supporters who can commit to making a small donation today to flip the Senate blue, please do. The majorities in both the House and the Senate will be won -- or lost on the margins.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/50f50d89-fef2-4e0a-888b-2ca9b761e46e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Finally, I want to leave you with this. These are hard, profoundly troubling times. But our country has faced moments like this before, and in each instance, freedom-loving people have reached down deep to find inner strength -- and then reached out far and wide to spread their faith in the American experiment. They've added more patriots to the cause and together, they've built a stronger, better country. America turns 250 years old this summer. And her call to action has never been stronger. We can do this too.
Thanks for all you do to support Democrats.
With every good wish,
Maggie Hassan

body:
This rescue was possible because people chose to act.

| | |
---
| |
---
| GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE
---
|
---
| | Friend,No one could hear her. A young girl named Kristen was locked in an attic. No windows. No fresh air. No way out. The door was locked from the outside. For months she lived there.
Alone. There was no bathroom.
Just a bucket. No shower. No clean clothes. And the only time she left that attic was when she was sold for sex.
Over. And over. And over. **This is the reality of child trafficking.**

Millions of children are trapped in exploitation around the world. But Kristen's story did not end in that attic. One night she knocked on a hotel room door. Her trafficker had arranged and forced her into another "date." But instead...**she met a rescue team - Freedom Strike Force. **They were working alongside law enforcement to identify victims and traffickers. When Kristen realized she was safe... She collapsed into the arms of one of our female advocates. **Free.** Law enforcement then raided the house where she was held. Traffickers were arrested. Kristen was taken to a safe place. For the first time in months, she had a real bed and a hot meal**.**

**She took the first step toward healing.** **This rescue was possible because people chose to act.**
---

The **Sound of Freedom Foundation** exists to _stop_ _ __the sale __of God 's children._ Inspired by the film _Sound of Freedom_ , the Foundation works around the world to **prevent trafficking, support rescue efforts, educate families, raise awareness, and push for stronger laws that protect children.** Our mission is simple. **To stop the sale of God 's children.** And right now we are preparing a new mission, happening in just a few weeks in Phoenix. Our **Freedom Strike Force** partner will train local law enforcement for two days, teaching them how to identify traffickers and victims hidden in plain sight. Then on day three...they go into the field. **Real operations. Real arrests. Real rescues.**

clean_body: This rescue was possible because people chose to act. | | | | | | GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE | | | Friend,No one could hear her. A young girl named Kristen was locked in an attic. No windows. No fresh air. No way out. The door was locked from the outside. For months she lived there. Alone. There was no bathroom. Just a bucket. No shower. No clean clothes. And the only time she left that attic was when she was sold for sex. Over. And over. And over. This is the reality of child trafficking. Millions of children are trapped in exploitation around the world. But Kristen's story did not end in that attic. One night she knocked on a hotel room door. Her trafficker had arranged and forced her into another "date." But instead...she met a rescue team - Freedom Strike Force. They were working alongside law enforcement to identify victims and traffickers. When Kristen realized she was safe... She collapsed into the arms of one of our female advocates. Free. Law enforcement then raided the house where she was held. Traffickers were arrested. Kristen was taken to a safe place. For the first time in months, she had a real bed and a hot meal. She took the first step toward healing. This rescue was possible because people chose to act. The Sound of Freedom Foundation exists to stop the sale of God 's children. Inspired by the film Sound of Freedom , the Foundation works around the world to prevent trafficking, support rescue efforts, educate families, raise awareness, and push for stronger laws that protect children. Our mission is simple. To stop the sale of God 's children. And right now we are preparing a new mission, happening in just a few weeks in Phoenix. Our Freedom Strike Force partner will train local law enforcement for two days, teaching them how to identify traffickers and victims hidden in plain sight. Then on day three...they go into the field. Real operations. Real arrests. Real rescues. | | | | | Children like Kristen are waiting. * * *
Former reality T.V. star Spencer Pratt made a grand impression during his debate with Mayor Karen Bass and Council member Nithya Raman as the race heats up for the race to be Los Angeles' mayor.
Pratt's momentum was building prior to his appearance on the debate stage. Through short, yet impactful campaign ads that are highlighting the competitions' failures to advocating for the end of the rampant dog abuse by drug addicts on Skid Row, along with Pratt's personal story of losing his home during the 2025 wildfires, he has not been holding back.
[| | | | | Spencer Pratt
---
@spencerpratt
| 3:03 PM * May 8, 2026 * 855K Views969 Replies * 5.9K Reposts * 31.9K Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/da409bb0-2168-415f-a007-4e8ceb2a8c2c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
That intense, constant barrage of hammering by Pratt has left Bass and Raman on the backfoot.
When asked for a yes or no response to if illegal aliens living in Los Angeles should be able to vote in local elections, Pratt was the only one who gave a quick and emphatic "No." Bass and Raman gave word salads to say that "it depends."
[| | | | | Libs of TikTok
---
@libsoftiktok
"Yes or no, should noncitizens be able to vote?" Spencer Pratt: No Karen Bass: It depends Nithya Raman: It depends This should tell you everything you need to know.
| 2:42 AM * May 7, 2026 * 1.35M Views1.22K Replies * 19.9K Reposts * 104K Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/8f7cdd0a-8c28-4952-96bc-23f2e8144b64?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
"If I wanna run against anybody, it would be the councilmember who is terrible," Pratt explained. "Mayor Bass has at least been a mayor for almost 4 years and has, as she talked about earlier, the unions, all the unions endorse Mayor Bass. Do you think it's easier to run against the incumbent mayor with all the unions or a random city council member who's been a failure for 6 years? I would much rather run against Councilwoman Raman!"
Raman could only muster a response that equated to, "Well, Pratt is a MAGA Republican" even though he has not prioritized national issues.
A UCLA Luskin poll taken before the debate **[showed Bass was in the lead at 25%,](https://substack.com/redirect/b4ac2f01-3fd6-4e27-9137-6ecc9750c7c7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** with Pratt in second place at 11%, and Raman at 9%. Up to 40% of voters are still undecided, meaning Bass' victory is far from a done deal.

_**(piece continues)**_
So if Pratt does what seems like the impossible, winning a race based on common sense instead of far-left nonsense in crazy blue L.A., could he actually turn it around?
I believe his administration will be similar to that of President Trump's second term. What he has the power to do in order to fix the basic things that need fixing, Pratt will move with lighting speed. The problems will emerge when it involves the city council, which Pratt can be sure he will not have many allies in.
Not to mention the union machine, which as previously mentioned is supporting Bass, will likely mobilize its members to run interference in their respective fields.
It is not an enviable position to be in. Yes, he's at the top but since he is the outsider, the forces within and without who want to go back to the status quo can be guaranteed to make his term a tough slog. He has even threatened to cut off the wasteful taxpayer spending to the NGOs. When money is on the line, who knows what tricks will be pulled?
It speaks volumes the bar for Pratt's campaign is so low, it basically boils down to:
* "I'll enforce the law!"

* "I'll stop the dog abuse by drug addicts!"

* "I'll actually prepare for wildfires!"

It is equally cynical to know many voters, not all, will see that and say, "Nice try, racist! No way!"
The rest of the country will have to wait and see if voters in Los Angeles have had enough of the purposeful decline.

| This is major news — and I wanted you to hear it directly from me.

**I’ve officially been added to the Democrats’ _Red to Blue program_ — a select group of competitive House candidates who have the best chance at flipping Republican-held seats.** [](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/108951?t=6&akid=24236%2E878179%2E3vhGnt) [I’ll explain more about what this means, but if you’re ready to help us build on this moment and take back the House, will you split $10 between the Voter Protection Project and me right now?](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/108951?t=7&akid=24236%2E878179%2E3vhGnt) | [Donate »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/108951?t=8&akid=24236%2E878179%2E3vhGnt)

We’re entering a new phase of this campaign — higher stakes, more attention, and a sharper contrast than ever before.

May 9, 2026

The media, the Democrats and some Black politicians are in an uproar because the Supreme Court decision, Louisiana vs Callais, made racial gerrymandering more difficult. But the good news for Blacks is now they have a chance to be represented by Black congressmen who share their values, not Black congressmen bankrolled by white liberals.
First some background. In the South, voting was once problematic for Blacks because literacy tests and poll taxes were required to register. This was rectified with the Voting Rights Act of 1965, which not only disallowed these abuses, but also mandated judicial review or "preclearance" for further legislation that could be construed to prevent Blacks from voting.

The problem is that this did not necessarily create more Blacks in Congress. Thus, the Supreme Court ruled in 1986 in Thornburg v. Gingles that districts had to be created in which Blacks could win elections, and this required placing a large number of Blacks in one district.

But this did not necessarily help the Democrats.

For example, Georgia in 1990, had ten Congressional districts and nine were held by white Democrats. Then Newt Gingrich sat down with the Black Democrats and said, "[Do I have a deal for you.](https://substack.com/redirect/76afc305-e404-49a5-bd79-0bfe8d1399d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" The result is that when the 1990 census gave Georgia another district, Gingrich and the Black Democrats constructed a map in which by 1992, there were three Black Democratic congressmen, one white Democratic congressman and seven Republican congressmen, resulting in happy Black Democrats, happy Republicans but livid white Democrats.
But in 2013, the Supreme court ruled in Shelby County v. Holder that preclearance was no longer necessary, and this leads us to Louisiana. The Republican lead legislature created a map that resulted in one Black district, but the Democratic Governor, John Bel Edwards, wanted two, so he vetoed it. This ended up in federal court and Edward's view prevailed. But the Supreme Court just overturned this decision, and Louisiana can now redraw its map and eliminate at least one Black district.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3b401913-bd56-485b-8403-f401fe7a9fd5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The two serpentine Black voting districts of Louisiana

But when the courts forced Black districts to be created, they did not force candidates to raise money only from the constituents of that district. Since many of the Blacks in these districts were poor, the money came from outside sources, that is white liberals.

Since Blacks vote overwhelmingly for Democrats, the new congressman was not determined in the general election, it was determined in the primary. And primaries for open seats have multiple candidates, up to a dozen. And who wins this primary? The one with the most cash.
Thus Blacks are now represented by the likes of Louisiana Congressman Troy Carter. In 2024, he raised over $1,000,000, 68% from PACs (Political Action Committees), 28% large contributions, and only $899 from contributions under $200 (0,08%)! This guy is bankrolled by corporations, white liberals and rich lawyers; his overwhelmingly poor Black constituency gives him next to nothing.

So, who does he represent? The overwhelmingly wealthy white liberals who finance him. For example, did you ever here of a Black father who wants his son to dress up like a girl? Of course not. Only [Westport Unitarians](https://substack.com/redirect/67e09a96-7927-4998-86c7-01c8f748ee36?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [Grade B Hollywood](https://substack.com/redirect/ae3913ce-faea-489e-87e9-0e8109ccad6d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) actors subject their children to this insanity. But Troy Carter is a great advocate of trans rights.

And Black Congressman dutifully blame Republicans for suppressing Black voters. But this biggest suppression of Black votes is through the disproportionate number of abortions on Black women. 13.5% of the country is Black but 35% of abortions are performed on Blacks. If the percentage was that of white women, there would be at least 15,000,000 more Black voters. It is hard to vote when you no longer exist.

But any Democratic Black congressman who had the guts to point this out would quickly find a Black primary opponent financed by rich white liberals. And he would be toast.

And look at this video of protestors against the Supreme Court decision.

[| | | | | The Tennessee Holler
---
@TheTNHoller
HAPPENING NOW... marching on the Capitol.... #NewJimCrow @GovBillLee
| 6:30 PM * May 5, 2026 * 236K Views912 Replies * 2.58K Reposts * 8.74K Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/f6358682-32a5-4c4f-a540-0135440934e1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Out of several hundred protestors, about a dozen are Black. There rest are all white liberals.
But what is really fascinating is watching this video of Tennessee State Representative Justin Pearson objecting to a majority Black district being gerrymandered.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/75b2afc3-a1fa-4123-bf5c-b0611875914d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

But let's look at the present Congressman of this district, Congressman Steve Cohan and the candidate, Charlotte Bergmann, who is favored to replace him due to this gerrymander.
Hmmm. What do you notice in the pictures below?
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d05c3330-61a3-4d85-b165-f82550683dbc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Congressman Steve Cohan of the majority Black district in Tennesee
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ddc93076-2b91-4d53-b51d-572b1bd25b7f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Congressman Steve Cohen's likely replacement Charlotte Bergmann

Either Representative Pearson is entirely bankrolled by white liberals, or he has the worst case of color blindness I have ever seen! And I have been practicing ophthalmologist for over forty years.

In the long run, Blacks will be better represented by Blacks who share their values, not the values of white liberals.

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: I don’t like wasting money, Peter.
body:
This is how I’ve lived my whole life, and how I’ll lead as Governor of Texas.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter, I want to tell you a little about how this campaign actually operates — because it says a lot about how I’ll lead as governor.
I’ve never believed in wasting money. That’s not a campaign talking point; it’s how I’ve lived my whole life. When you grow up watching every dollar, you learn quickly that money represents someone’s time, sacrifice, and trust.
That mindset shapes every decision we make.
We’re building a campaign powered by people, not billionaires.
We focus on what helps us win: organizing communities, talking directly with voters, and showing up everywhere — not just where it’s convenient.

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | | On August 7th President Trump signed Executive Order #14330. The Court’s cruel ruling in _Louisiana v. Callais_ is a direct hit to the heart of the Voting Rights Act and the fragile promise that every American’s vote should carry equal weight.
Until the Voting Rights Act, the 15th Amendment — which barred the federal government and the states from denying the right to vote based on race, color, and servitude — was routinely ignored by Southern states using the legal mechanism of Jim Crow.
Poll taxes, literacy tests, and language restrictions were the most visible tools of voter suppression.
But hostile political regimes also drew the boundaries of voting lines and districts to make it impossible for Black and brown voters to elect anyone who represented their interests.
Enter the Voting Rights Act.
Section 2 of that act made it illegal to design districts to dilute or block racial communities from finding common cause. It also required a corrective action.
But now the _Callais_ decision has dramatically narrowed that core protection against racially discriminatory redistricting.
**The consequences of this disastrous ruling are already reverberating across our country.**
Majority-Black districts could be dismantled or diluted. Latino districts in fast-growing areas could lose political muscle. Representatives championing the minority communities they represent will likely lose their seats. Congressional maps in closely divided states could be tilted further away from competitiveness.
**But the Roberts Court is not the only actor in this story. Alongside groups like Fair Fight Action, we can continue the fight for multiracial democracy. We can continue calling for reforms that ensure equal representation in the halls of power.**
Congress retains the authority to strengthen voting rights protections. State legislatures can adopt independent redistricting commissions or refuse to vote for racially discriminatory maps. Voters can reach out to elected officials at every level of government and demand that they publicly take a stand for voting rights. Civic organizations can mobilize communities to solve for voter suppression tactics even when the rules shift.
**Fair Fight Action will continue pushing this vital work forward.**
As the Roberts Court considered Callais, Fair Fight Action laid bare the stakes of the case by identifying how gutting Section 2 could secure enough safe Republican seats to lock in one-party rule for a generation.
**Now the team is mobilizing advocates across the country. Just this past weekend, Fair Fight Action directly contacted our communities in Tennessee, Louisiana, and Alabama. And collectively, we are rallying a movement behind fair elections with fair maps, pressing forward for proactive voting rights protections at the state and national level, working to mitigate the effects of voter suppression attempts, and fighting to reverse the authoritarian playbook.**

# The TTV Weekly Wrap Up
---
| This week continued last week's rage on the redistricting battlefield. A quick look back: on April 27, the Supreme Court upheld Texas's redrawn congressional map — a 6-3 decision expected to deliver Republicans up to five additional House seats in the Lone Star state. Two days later, the Court handed down _Louisiana v. Callais_ , ending the race-based districting that had been a defining element of the Voting Rights Act since its passage over sixty years ago, in a very different America. Together, the two rulings have unleashed a wave of redrawing across the country. Florida moved within an hour of _Callais_. Louisiana suspended its May 16 primary so it could redraw. The Tennessee House has already approved a new map. Alabama and South Carolina are right behind. The American congressional map is being redrawn under voters' feet, in real time. To understand why, you have to start in 1965. The Voting Rights Act, passed in '65, created two enforcement mechanisms. Section 2 was a nationwide prohibition on voting practices that discriminated by race. Section 5 was more aggressive — it required select jurisdictions to "preclear" any change to their election laws with the federal government before it took effect. Move a polling place. Add a voter ID rule. Redraw a district line. Under preclearance, the state or county had to ask Washington first. In 2013, the Supreme Court ended that regime. _Shelby County v. Holder_ struck down the coverage formula, holding that Congress could not run preclearance in the twenty-first century based on formulas used in 1965 — and inviting Congress to write a new standard based on current data. Congress didn't, so Section 5 effectively went dormant. But President Obama saw an opportunity. By January 2017, immediately upon leaving the White House, Barack Obama and his former Attorney General Eric Holder had launched a national operation aimed at one thing: controlling who draws the maps. Not winning elections — drawing the maps. The [National Democratic Redistricting Committee (NDRC)](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/n4uz4vr7xohvhxpv0rvh6h647p7rmflhqvn23/p8heh9h4oq22mrcq/ZGVtb2NyYXRpY3JlZGlzdHJpY3RpbmcuY29t), chaired by Holder, quickly raised over a hundred million dollars and went to work in three places: state legislative races, ballot initiatives to install so-called "independent" redistricting commissions, and litigation under every flag that fit. The lawyer at the center of it was Marc Elias, then at Perkins Coie, later the founder of both the Elias Law Group and Democracy Docket (the media operation that simultaneously reports on and shapes the narrative around the very lawsuits his firm files.) For nearly a decade, the NDRC argued that race had to be the central organizing principle of every congressional map in America. Then on April 29, 2026, the Supreme Court handed down _Callais_ — 6-3. The Court held that race-conscious redistricting runs into the Equal Protection Clause and the Fifteenth Amendment, and that states almost never have a compelling interest sufficient to justify it. In plain English: you cannot use race as the predominant factor when you draw a district. The reaction was immediate. Six states had already enacted new mid-decade maps before _Callais_ — North Carolina, Missouri, Ohio, Utah, Texas, and Virginia. Florida, Louisiana, Alabama, Tennessee, and South Carolina are now racing to follow. On the Democratic side, Governor Kathy Hochul has vowed a constitutional amendment to redraw New York. Hakeem Jeffries has named Maryland and Illinois as targets. Maryland passed its own state Voting Rights Act twenty-four hours before _Callais_ came down, and Governor Wes Moore has stood up a redistricting advisory commission to consider new boundaries. Legal challenges are already piling up. The Purcell principle, which limits how late federal courts can change election rules before an election, will determine how much of this is actually in place by November. Top political forecasters estimate Republicans will pick up 5 to 10 House seats from the redistricting wars; the high end could reach 13 to 19. In a House where the majority has been decided by a handful of seats in each of the last three cycles, that is a structural shift. Here is where this leaves us. Both parties are now drawing maps for naked partisan advantage. The pretenses are dropping on both sides. The underlying machinery is the same. In one sense, that's an improvement. Sorting voters by skin color and packing them into districts was always a constitutional embarrassment dressed up as civil rights. _Callais_ ended that. But honesty in the rationale is not the same as good representation. A brazenly partisan map can still produce a House where most members never face a competitive election, and where most voters live in a district whose outcome was settled in a state legislature five years earlier. The only check on either party's worst impulses is informed citizens showing up — at the state house, the county clerk's office, the local board — and refusing to look away. If you want to see the voting-rights landscape this story is reshaping, we've built an [interactive map](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/n4uz4vr7xohvhxpv0rvh6h647p7rmflhqvn23/x0hph6he0qppoof5/aHR0cHM6Ly9tYWdpY2FsLW1hbGFiaS03ZmM0OWYubmV0bGlmeS5hcHAv) showing where federal preclearance coverage, same-day voter registration, and post-_Callais_ redistricting all overlap, state by state. We also tracked Louisiana's mapping efforts, covered a new conviction in a New Jersey voter fraud case, and got the scoop on the DOJ's expanding investigation into Fulton County's 2020 election operations — plus podcasts, apps, and more. Check it out 👇

The DOJ [issued](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/n4uz4vr7xohvhxpv0rvh6h647p7rmflhqvn23/25h2hoh3wm886pf3/aHR0cHM6Ly9hY3JvYmF0LmFkb2JlLmNvbS9pZC91cm46YWFpZDpzYzpVUzo5YzVhMzJkMC0zNDFjLTQ2YmYtODYxZS04MGQ0N2NjZTBhZTI_dmlld2VyJTIxbWVnYVZlcmI9Z3JvdXAtZGlzY292ZXI=) a grand jury subpoena seeking information on everyone involved in Fulton's 2020 election operations. clean_body: Truth, prayer, and action — all in one place. | | May 09, 2026 | == | | | | The TTV Weekly Wrap Up | This week continued last week's rage on the redistricting battlefield. A quick look back: on April 27, the Supreme Court upheld Texas's redrawn congressional map — a 6-3 decision expected to deliver Republicans up to five additional House seats in the Lone Star state. Two days later, the Court handed down Louisiana v. Callais , ending the race-based districting that had been a defining element of the Voting Rights Act since its passage over sixty years ago, in a very different America. Together, the two rulings have unleashed a wave of redrawing across the country. Florida moved within an hour of Callais. Louisiana suspended its May 16 primary so it could redraw. The Tennessee House has already approved a new map. Alabama and South Carolina are right behind. The American congressional map is being redrawn under voters' feet, in real time. To understand why, you have to start in 1965. The Voting Rights Act, passed in '65, created two enforcement mechanisms. Section 2 was a nationwide prohibition on voting practices that discriminated by race. Section 5 was more aggressive — it required select jurisdictions to "preclear" any change to their election laws with the federal government before it took effect. Move a polling place. Add a voter ID rule. Redraw a district line. Under preclearance, the state or county had to ask Washington first. In 2013, the Supreme Court ended that regime. Shelby County v. Holder struck down the coverage formula, holding that Congress could not run preclearance in the twenty-first century based on formulas used in 1965 — and inviting Congress to write a new standard based on current data. Congress didn't, so Section 5 effectively went dormant. But President Obama saw an opportunity. By January 2017, immediately upon leaving the White House, Barack Obama and his former Attorney General Eric Holder had launched a national operation aimed at one thing: controlling who draws the maps. Not winning elections — drawing the maps. The , chaired by Holder, quickly raised over a hundred million dollars and went to work in three places: state legislative races, ballot initiatives to install so-called "independent" redistricting commissions, and litigation under every flag that fit. The lawyer at the center of it was Marc Elias, then at Perkins Coie, later the founder of both the Elias Law Group and Democracy Docket (the media operation that simultaneously reports on and shapes the narrative around the very lawsuits his firm files.) For nearly a decade, the NDRC argued that race had to be the central organizing principle of every congressional map in America. Then on April 29, 2026, the Supreme Court handed down Callais — 6-3. The Court held that race-conscious redistricting runs into the Equal Protection Clause and the Fifteenth Amendment, and that states almost never have a compelling interest sufficient to justify it. In plain English: you cannot use race as the predominant factor when you draw a district. The reaction was immediate. Six states had already enacted new mid-decade maps before Callais — North Carolina, Missouri, Ohio, Utah, Texas, and Virginia. Florida, Louisiana, Alabama, Tennessee, and South Carolina are now racing to follow. On the Democratic side, Governor Kathy Hochul has vowed a constitutional amendment to redraw New York. Hakeem Jeffries has named Maryland and Illinois as targets. Maryland passed its own state Voting Rights Act twenty-four hours before Callais came down, and Governor Wes Moore has stood up a redistricting advisory commission to consider new boundaries. Legal challenges are already piling up. The Purcell principle, which limits how late federal courts can change election rules before an election, will determine how much of this is actually in place by November. Top political forecasters estimate Republicans will pick up 5 to 10 House seats from the redistricting wars; the high end could reach 13 to 19. In a House where the majority has been decided by a handful of seats in each of the last three cycles, that is a structural shift. Here is where this leaves us. Both parties are now drawing maps for naked partisan advantage. The pretenses are dropping on both sides. The underlying machinery is the same. In one sense, that's an improvement. Sorting voters by skin color and packing them into districts was always a constitutional embarrassment dressed up as civil rights. Callais ended that. But honesty in the rationale is not the same as good representation. A brazenly partisan map can still produce a House where most members never face a competitive election, and where most voters live in a district whose outcome was settled in a state legislature five years earlier. The only check on either party's worst impulses is informed citizens showing up — at the state house, the county clerk's office, the local board — and refusing to look away. If you want to see the voting-rights landscape this story is reshaping, we've built an showing where federal preclearance coverage, same-day voter registration, and post-Callais redistricting all overlap, state by state. We also tracked Louisiana's mapping efforts, covered a new conviction in a New Jersey voter fraud case, and got the scoop on the DOJ's expanding investigation into Fulton County's 2020 election operations — plus podcasts, apps, and more. | | I chaired the first-ever Congressional hearing on the abortion medication, mifepristone. I started leading the charge to help get this medication onto the market. I can't believe that all these years later, we are still having to fight the same battle again against Republicans that want to rip away access to this mainstay of reproductive health care. Last week, anti-freedom forces scored an unfortunate victory when a federal appeals court (stacked with Republican-appointed judges) _blocked_ people's ability to receive mifepristone by mail. The extremists propelling this case forward relied on a dangerous practice known as "judge shopping," when activist plaintiffs guarantee their case will be heard by judges they know will rule in their favor. **Thus, they're able to interfere with the private health care decisions of Americans even in states where abortion remains legal, like Oregon.** The Supreme Court has temporarily stayed the appeal court's decision, but it will eventually issue a broader ruling — and based on their recent actions, there's little reason for optimism. Moreover, the case should _never_ have gotten this far to begin with. **This case is about one thing and one thing only: Republicans' perverse obsession with controlling women's bodies and our most private health care decisions.** This should be about science and privacy, not politics. We need to restore abortion rights protections across the country, _and_ we need to fix our judiciary so that extremists can't game the system. There's a lot of work ahead of us, and noneof it will get done without a Senate majority. [**That's why I need your help to flip the chamber in November. subject: To my favorite patriot in FL
body:
I’m so proud to be in this with you.

| | | | Peter,
They call us “radicals.”
They call us “extremists.”
They call us “deplorables.”
The media mocks us. The Hollywood elites look down on us. The D.C. swamp tries to break us every single day.
But when I look at you, Peter, I don’t see any of that,

I see a patriot.
I see a hero who works hard, loves their family, and stands up for what is right, even when it’s not popular.
I see someone with a spine of steel who loves this country too much to let it go. I don't say this enough, but I am so incredibly proud to be in this fight with you.
I wanted to send you this personal message as a small token of my appreciation. Something to remind you that you are seen, you are valued, and you are vital to saving America. | [ ACCEPT MY THANKS >> ](https://trk.emails.marshablackburn.)
---
Thank you for being the best part of my job.

With gratitude,

Marsha Blackburn

clean_body: That's the Mayor of Los Angeles. Throwing up her hands. Admitting that after years in office, billions of dollars spent, and thousands of Angelenos still living on the streets — she has nothing to show for it.This is my competition? Peter, I'm going to let Karen Bass speak for herself on this one. While talking about the homeless crisis destroying neighborhoods across Los Angeles, the Mayor of this city — the woman who has been in charge — looked into the camera and said: "Nothing works." That's it. That's the Mayor of Los Angeles. Throwing up her hands. Admitting that after years in office, billions of dollars spent, and thousands of Angelenos still living on the streets — she has nothing to show for it. | But it gets better... She then turned around and attacked the very field workers who are out there every single day, actually trying to help people. The people doing the hard work while she was on a plane to Ghana. She told them — experts who have dedicated their careers to this crisis — that they don't know the people they're serving. What?!!!!!!! Karen Bass doesn't know what works. Karen Bass doesn't trust the people doing the work. And Karen Bass just admitted both of those things out loud. That’s my competition. I didn't go to politician school. I don't have a thirty-year career in government to protect. What I have is a burned lot where my home used to be, a city I love that is falling apart, and the common sense to know that when nothing works — it’s up to you to change everything. New leadership. New accountability. New results. Los Angeles cannot afford four more years of a Mayor who looks at the worst crisis in this city's history and shrugs. This is exactly why I'm running. body:
We’re running out of time to reach voters.
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21486?t=1&akid=41287%2E3422442%2Ewa44dW)
Peter,
There’s a terrifying reality in the California governor’s race:
With less than a month until the primary election, if we don’t consolidate support now, two MAGA Republicans could lock Democrats out of the general election ballot.
**We need a Democrat who stands out from the pack.** I’m not like most people running for governor. I'm a single mom of three kids who fills the gas tank and pushes the grocery cart just like almost everybody else in our state — and most of all, I can take accountability and laugh at myself too.
**That’s why we made the decision to launch a new ad—to cut through the noise and make sure voters across California hear what’s at stake.[You can check it out here:](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_kp_20260509_3_ak.oMgMHk&refcode=em20260509-41287&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=41287%2E3422442%2Ewa44dW)**
[](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_kp_20260509_3_ak.oMgMHk&refcode=em20260509-41287&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=4&akid=41287%2E3422442%2Ewa44dW)
I’m running to lower costs for working families and take on powerful interests that keep Californians stuck—but none of that matters if voters don’t hear our message before ballots are cast.
And right now, that means breaking through a flood of spending from corporate-funded candidates and a literal billionaire pouring money into this race.
That’s why we launched this ad. Now, we need to keep it on air for as long as possible. California media markets are among the most expensive in the country, and with only weeks left until the primary, every day counts.
I’m counting on supporters like you, Peter, to help us keep this message in front of voters when it matters most.
**[I’d be honored if you chipped in $5 today to help us keep this ad on air and reach as many Californians as possible before the primary.](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_kp_20260509_3_ak.oMgMHk&refcode=em20260509-41287&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=5&akid=41287%2E3422442%2Ewa44dW)**

Thank you,
Katie

Katie is running to be California’s next governor because California and our country need a leader who will stand up to Trump to lower costs, protect our rights, and combat climate change. **[Donate ›››](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/kp4g-em-footer?refcode=em20260509-41287&amounts=&t=25&refcode2=41287_3422442_wa44dW&akid=41287%2E3422442%2Ewa44dW)**

That’s why we made the decision to launch a new ad—to cut through the noise and make sure voters across California hear what’s at stake. I’m running to lower costs for working families and take on powerful interests that keep Californians stuck—but none of that matters if voters don’t hear our message before ballots are cast. And right now, that means breaking through a flood of spending from corporate-funded candidates and a literal billionaire pouring money into this race. That’s why we launched this ad. Now, we need to keep it on air for as long as possible. California media markets are among the most expensive in the country, and with only weeks left until the primary, every day counts. I’m counting on supporters like you, Peter, to help us keep this message in front of voters when it matters most. Thank you, Katie Katie is running to be California’s next governor because California and our country need a leader who will stand up to Trump to lower costs, protect our rights, and combat climate change.
